## §8.2.2: Exterior Differential $\dtilde$, Poincaré Integral $\Izero$ & Carnap 8.1 {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: EXTERIOR DIFFERENTIAL &amp; POINCARÉ HOMOTOPY INTEGRAL (DEF. 8.5) &amp; CARNAP SCHOLIUM 8.1</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 8.5: Exterior Differential & Poincaré Homotopy Integral on Corners**
Let $\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$ and $C_{\mathbf{0}}^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n) \coloneqq \{f \in C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n) \mid f(\mathbf{0}) = 0\}$.
1. **Whitney Closed Bounded 1-Forms $\Omega_{\mathrm{closed},b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n)$:** Smooth 1-forms $\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n \omega_i(x)\,dx^i$ on $(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$ (smooth up to the boundary in the sense of Whitney) satisfying $d\omega = 0$.
2. **Infinitesimal Differential Functor $\dtilde \colon C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n) \to \Omega_{\mathrm{closed},b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n)$:**
$$
\dtilde f \;\coloneqq\; df \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \left(\parttilde_i| f\right) dx^i \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^i} dx^i \tag{SM-30}
$$
where $\parttilde_i| f(x) \coloneqq \lim_{\Delta x^i \to 0^+} \frac{f(x + \Delta x^i e_i) - f(x)}{\Delta x^i}$.
3. **Poincaré Homotopy Integral Functor $\Izero \colon \Omega_{\mathrm{closed},b}^1(\mathcal{M}_n) \to C^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n)$:** Integrates $\omega$ along the radial ray $\gamma_x(t) = tx$ ($t \in [0,1]$) from $\mathbf{0} \in \mathcal{M}_n$:
$$
\left(\Izero\,\omega\right)(x) \;\coloneqq\; \int_0^1 \sum_{i=1}^n x^i \omega_i(tx)\,dt
$$
satisfying path-independence and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus on the star-shaped octant $\mathcal{M}_n$ for any smooth path $\gamma \colon [a,b] \to \mathcal{M}_n$:
$$
\dtilde\left(\Izero\,\omega\right) = \omega, \qquad \Izero(\dtilde f)(x) = f(x) - f(\mathbf{0}), \qquad \mathrm{I}_a^b(\dtilde f) = f(\gamma(b)) - f(\gamma(a)) \tag{SM-33}
$$
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Carnap 8.1: Synthetic Infinitesimals (Kock–Lawvere) vs. Discrete Metronics**
In **Synthetic Differential Geometry** (SDG; Kock 1981, Lawvere 1979), differentiation is formalized algebraically inside a smooth topos via square-zero infinitesimals $D \coloneqq \llbracket d \in R \mid d^2 = 0 \rrbracket \subset R$ with $\forall d \in D,\; f(x+d) = f(x) + f'(x)d$.
$$
\boxed{\text{SDG provides an internal infinitesimal calculus; DEC provides a discrete cochain calculus.}}
$$
These are distinct mathematical architectures and modeling strata ($\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{C}$); constructing a formal or functorial bridge is a separate reconstruction problem, not a deductive identity.
:::

:::

## §8.3.1: Corner Smoothness & Seeley Extension Operator (Thm. 8.6) {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: WHY NAIVE APPROACHES FAIL II, SEELEY EXTENSION ON CORNERS (THM. 8.6 PART 1 &amp; FIG. 8.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.firewall-box}
**Why Naive Approaches Fail II: Boundary Smoothness at a Corner**
* A **zero extension** across $x=0$ preserves smoothness only when every boundary derivative vanishes; for $e^{-x}$ on $x \ge 0$, $f(0^+) = 1 \ne 0$, so zero extension is discontinuous.
* **Even reflection** $e^{-|x|}$ is continuous, but has a jump in its first derivative at $x=0$ ($f'(0^+) = -1 \ne f'(0^-) = +1$), destroying Schwartz seminorms $\|f\|_{\alpha,\beta}$.
* **Resolution:** Robert Seeley's (1964) extension operator constructs a moment-matched linear combination of dyadically rescaled reflections across each boundary hyperplane, preserving all Schwartz seminorms on corners!
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 8.6 (Part 1): Multidimensional Seeley Extension on Corners (Fig. 8.2)**
Let $\mathcal{M}_n \coloneqq (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$ (with $R_n(\mathbb{C}) \cong \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ in real Cartesian coordinates). Following Seeley (1964), let $\chi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ satisfy $\chi(t)=1$ for $|t|\le 1$ and $\chi(t)=0$ for $|t|\ge 2$, and let $(a_k)_{k=0}^\infty$ be a rapidly decreasing sequence ($\sum_{k=0}^\infty |a_k| 2^{km} < \infty$ $\forall m \in \mathbb{N}_0$) satisfying the **Vandermonde moment identities**:
$$
\sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k (-2^k)^m \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall m \in \mathbb{N}_0
$$
Then the coordinatewise extension $\mathcal{E}_{x_i} f(x_i) \coloneqq \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k \chi(-2^k x_i) f(-2^k x_i)$ ($x_i < 0$) and its tensor product $\mathcal{E}^{(n)} \coloneqq \bigotimes_{i=1}^n \mathcal{E}_{x_i} \colon \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n) \to \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ define a continuous linear right-inverse to restriction $\mathcal{R}_+ \colon \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n) \twoheadrightarrow \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n)$:
$$
\mathcal{R}_+ \circ \mathcal{E}^{(n)} \;=\; \operatorname{id}_{\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)}, \qquad P \coloneqq \mathcal{E}^{(n)} \circ \mathcal{R}_+ \;=\; P^2
$$
:::

## §8.3.1: Grothendieck Nuclear Variable Separation & Proof (Thm. 8.6) {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: GROTHENDIECK NUCLEARITY ON CORNERS (THM. 8.6 PARTS 2–4, FIG. 8.1), FULL PROOF &amp; TOY EXAMPLE</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 8.6 (Parts 2–4): Nuclearity Inheritance & Tensor Expansion (Fig. 8.1)**
* **Nuclearity Inheritance:** Because $\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n)$ is isomorphic via $\mathcal{E}^{(n)}$ to the closed complemented subspace $\operatorname{Im}(\mathcal{E}^{(n)} \circ \mathcal{R}_+) \subset \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, it inherits nuclearity from $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ (Grothendieck 1955; Ryan 2002):
$$
\mathscr{S}\!\left((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m\right) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{l=1}^{m,\pi} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{l=1}^{m,\varepsilon} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})
$$
* **Projective Tensor Expansion:** Every rapid-decay synkolation kernel $f \in \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)$ admits an absolutely convergent projective tensor expansion into 1D factors with bounded $\{\phi_j^{(l)}\} \subset \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})$:
$$
f(x_1, \dots, x_m) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^\infty \lambda_j \, \phi_j^{(1)}(x_1) \otimes \dots \otimes \phi_j^{(m)}(x_m), \qquad \sum_{j=1}^\infty |\lambda_j| < \infty
$$
* **Claim Ceiling ($c_{\mathrm{NUCL}}$):** Grothendieck nuclearity guarantees an *absolutely convergent series* of separated tensor products in $\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)$; finite-rank (single-product) ODE separability holds iff the kernel has tensor rank $1$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 8.6 & Toy Example ($f(x_1,x_2) = e^{-(x_1+x_2)}\cos(x_1 x_2)$):**
1. **Step 1 (Derivative Matching):** Differentiating $\mathcal{E}_{x_i} f$ term-by-term for $x_i < 0$ via $\sum |a_k| 2^{km} < \infty$ yields $\lim_{x_i \to 0^-} \partial_{x_i}^m(\mathcal{E}_{x_i}f) = (\sum a_k(-2^k)^m)\partial_{x_i}^m f(0^+) = \partial_{x_i}^m f(0^+)$, preserving all Schwartz seminorms $\|\cdot\|_{\alpha,\beta}$.
2. **Step 2 (Idempotent Retract):** $P = \mathcal{E}^{(n)} \circ \mathcal{R}_+$ satisfies $P^2 = P$, identifying $\mathscr{S}(\mathcal{M}_n)$ with the closed subspace $\operatorname{Im}(P) \subset \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$.
3. **Step 3 (Nuclear Permanence):** Closed subspaces of nuclear Fréchet spaces are nuclear (Grothendieck 1955), yielding the series expansion. $\blacksquare$
* **Toy Example (Remark):** $f(x_1,x_2) = e^{-(x_1+x_2)}\cos(x_1 x_2) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^k}{(2k)!}(x_1^{2k}e^{-x_1})\otimes(x_2^{2k}e^{-x_2})$ with $\sum_{k=0}^\infty |\lambda_k| = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(2k)!} = \cosh(1) \approx 1.543 < \infty$.
:::

:::

## §8.3.2: Homometral Reducibility & Polarization on $\Sym^m(V)$ {.smaller transition="concave"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: POLARIZATION SCHOLIUM 8.7, HOMOMETRAL REDUCIBILITY THEOREM 8.8, PROOF &amp; CUBIC TOY EXAMPLE</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.scholium-box}
**Scholium 8.7 (Polarization and Effective Arity):**
Polarization reconstructs the multilinear form hidden by repeated inputs. Consequently, homometral sampling can be reduced to the genuinely distinct channels that carry new information, clarifying why effective arity may be smaller than nominal arity.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 8.8: Homometral Reduction in Symmetric Polynomial Envelopes**
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional real vector space with basis $\{e_1, \dots, e_n\}$ and $\Sym^m(V)$ the $m$-th symmetric tensor power.
1. **Polarization Identity:** Every element $v^m \in \Sym^m(V)$ generated by repeated (homometral) evaluation of $v = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i e_i$ decomposes uniquely into a linear combination of distinct (heterometral) symmetrized tensor products:
$$
v^m \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^m \sum_{1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n} c_{i_1 \dots i_k} \left( e_{i_1} \odot \dots \odot e_{i_k} \right)
$$
2. **Arity Reduction:** For any polynomial operadic functional $F \in \Oquant$ of nominal arity $m$ evaluated on $k < m$ distinct coordinates with multiplicities $(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ ($\sum a_j = m$), there exists a unique reduced operator $F_{\mathrm{red}} \in \Oquant(k; 1)$ of strict arity $k$ such that:
$$
F(\underbrace{x_1, \dots, x_1}_{a_1}, \dots, \underbrace{x_k, \dots, x_k}_{a_k}) \;=\; F_{\mathrm{red}}(x_1, \dots, x_k)
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Proof of Theorem 8.8 & Cubic Toy Example ($m=3, k=2$):**
* **Proof:** By the classical multilinear polarization identity, $P(v) = v^m$ is uniquely reconstructed from $m$ distinct slots via:
$$
\Pol(v_1, \dots, v_m) \;=\; \frac{1}{2^m m!} \sum_{\epsilon \in \{-1, 1\}^m} \left(\prod_{i=1}^m \epsilon_i\right) \left( \sum_{j=1}^m \epsilon_j v_j \right)^m
$$
When the input tuple contains only $k < m$ distinct variables, grouping identical slots collapses the summation domain onto a $k$-ary operator $F_{\mathrm{red}} \colon V^{\otimes k} \to W$ of strict effective arity $k < m$. $\blacksquare$
* **Cubic Toy Example:** A tertiary Synkolator ($m=3$) evaluating $F(x_1, x_1, x_2) = x_1^2 x_2$ (multiplicities $a_1=2, a_2=1$) reduces to $F_{\mathrm{red}}(u,v) \coloneqq u^2 v \in \Oquant(2;1)$ of strict binary arity $k = 2 < 3$ (SM, p. 133).
:::

:::

## §8.3.3: The Algebraic 15-to-3 Corporate Class Collapse & Lean 4 {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: 15-TO-3 CORPORATE COLLAPSE THEOREM 8.9, PROOF &amp; KERNEL-CHECKED LEAN 4 MODULE (S₂)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 8.9: Algebraic Collapse of Corporate Classes in $\Ctxquant$**
Let $\mathcal{S}_a, \mathcal{S}_b \in \Synquant$ be quantitative Syntrix algebras over parameter manifolds $R_{n_a}, R_{n_b}$ valued in a coefficient field $\mathbb{K} \in \Coeff$.
1. **Identification of Carrier & Functional Tiers:** Because every quantitative Synkolator $f \in \Oquant$ is a $\mathbb{K}$-valued functional operator evaluated directly on the coordinates of $R_n$ via the ring operations of $\mathbb{K}$, the synkolative rule selection ($K_s, C_s$) cannot vary independently of the metrophoric carrier selection ($K_m, C_m$): an uncoupled carrier coproduct forces block-diagonal functional composition, while carrier coordinate coupling forces functional cross-modulation.
2. **15-to-3 Class Reduction:** Restricting the $2 \times 2$ corporate rule matrix $\left\{\begin{smallmatrix} K_s & C_s \\ K_m & C_m \end{smallmatrix}\right\}$ to synchronized column selections ($K \coloneqq \{K_m, K_s\}$ and $C \coloneqq \{C_m, C_s\}$) collapses the $2^4 - 1 = 15$ general corporate classes (Ch. 3) to the $2^2 - 1 = \mathbf{3}$ non-empty subsets of $\{K, C\}$ (SM, pp. 133–135):
$$
\operatorname{Op}_{\mathrm{quant}} \;=\; \Big\{\; \mathbf{Kor}_{\{K\}} \ (\text{Pure Coupled}), \;\; \mathbf{Kor}_{\{C\}} \ (\text{Pure Parallel}), \;\; \mathbf{Kor}_{\{K, C\}} \ (\text{Partial Coupling + Composition}) \;\Big\}
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 8.9:**
In the qualitative category $\mathbf{Syn}$ (Ch. 3), $\{K_m, C_m\}$ and $\{K_s, C_s\}$ can be chosen independently ($2^4 - 1 = 15$ subsets). In $\Synquant$, every syndrome section $A_\gamma \in \Gamma_b^0(R_m, T^{\otimes k}R_m)$ is a function of the base parameter manifold $R_m$. If $R_{m_a}, R_{m_b}$ share $\lambda > 0$ coupled coordinates in the pushout $R_{m_a} \boxplus_\phi R_{m_b}$, evaluating functional operators across shared coordinates automatically induces synkolative coupling $K_s$; on uncoupled summands ($\lambda = 0$), operators act in parallel ($C_s$). Thus the active corporate rule is determined by a non-empty subset of $\{K, C\}$, yielding $2^2 - 1 = 3$ classes. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §8.5: Physical & Epistemic Sanity Checks & Carnapian Explication 8.1 {.smaller transition="convex"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Three Physical & Epistemic Sanity Checks (§8.5):**

1. **Leibniz Product Derivation Consistency:**
   Evaluating the differential functor $\dtilde$ on a product section $f \cdot g \in C_b^\infty(\mathcal{M}_n)$:
   $$
   \dtilde(f \cdot g) \;=\; d(fg) \;=\; f\,dg + g\,df \;=\; f \cdot (\dtilde g) + g \cdot (\dtilde f)
   $$
   which proves that the continuous differential functor strictly recovers the standard Leibniz derivation rule before passing to discrete metronic difference calculus (where a finite lattice cross-term $-\tau (\nabla u)(\nabla v)$ emerges in Chapter 10).

2. **Ring Element Invariance Check:**
   For any section $f \in \mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{M}_n)$, the zero and unity identities hold globally:
   $$
   f \cdot 0_{\mathcal{A}} = 0_{\mathcal{A}}, \qquad f \cdot 1_{\mathcal{A}} = f, \qquad f + 0_{\mathcal{A}} = f
   $$
   confirming that the parameter space $R_n$ preserves the exact algebraic field properties of $\mathbb{K}$.

3. **Nuclear Tensor Completion Uniqueness:**
   Because $\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})$ is nuclear, the topological tensor completions satisfy:
   $$
   \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \;=\; \widehat{\otimes}_\varepsilon
   $$
   Hence, variable separation is independent of the choice of cross-norm topology, guaranteeing that decomposed physical parameter channels are frame-invariant.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.carnap-box .fragment .zoom-in}

* **2. Explicatum (Stratum A/B):**
  The category of cornered parameter manifolds $\Manparam$, the Seeley extension operator $\mathcal{E}^{(n)}$ and Grothendieck nuclear tensor isomorphism $\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m) \cong \otpi \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})$, the exterior derivative $d$ and Poincaré homotopy integral $\Izero$, multilinear polarization (Theorem 8.8), and the synchronized column reduction $2^4 - 1 \to 2^2 - 1 = 3$ (Theorem 8.9).

**Historical Vignette (*The Stuttgart Astronautical Address*) & Switchboard Intuition:**
Historical discussions of Heim's manuscripts belong to the period's wider search for algebraic field symmetries; here they serve as context only, while the gauge constructions below stand on their own formal definitions. The symmetric, skew, cross-dimensional, and internal blocks of a $6\times 6$ metric act as channels on one **geometric switchboard**, where different physical roles correspond to typed blocks of the same tensor object.

* **From Coordinate Channels to Unified Spacetime:** Chapter 8 showed that continuous parameters on $\mathcal{M}_n = (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$ decompose via Grothendieck nuclearity. Yet macroscopic geometry cannot emerge in a single unmediated burst without infinite curvature stresses.
* **Strukturkaskade (SM §7.5, pp. 180–183):** Spacetime geometry is the convergent fixed point of a hierarchical assembly indexed by cascade tiers $\kaskadenstufe \in \{1, \dots, M\}$:
  * **Kaskadenbasis ($\kaskadenstufe = 1$):** Ensemble of $L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1}$ basal partial metrics ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(\gamma_1)}^{(1)}$ generated by tier $F_1$ of the *Quantitätssyntrix* on $R_n$.
  * **Partialkomposition (SM Eq. 60, p. 182):** Non-linear assembly integrating Christoffel connections and curvature couplings:
    $$
    {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(\gamma_\alpha)}^{(\alpha)} = \mathfrak{f}\!\left[ \left( {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(\gamma_{\alpha-1})}^{(\alpha-1)} \right)^{\omega_\alpha} \right], \quad 1 \le \gamma_\alpha \le L_\alpha = \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}, \quad 1 \le \alpha \le M \tag{SM-60}
    $$
  * **Kaskadenspitze ($\kaskadenstufe = M$, SM Eq. 60a):** Terminates at $L_M = 1, \omega_M = \omega = n/2$ into the unified metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$ via an **analytischer Syllogismus** (SM, p. 180) of ascending conditionality (*Bedingtheit*).

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proposition 9.1 (Closed-Form Sieve State Partition, SM Eqs. 59 & 59a):**
With sieve-state sum $(\omega - p)' \coloneqq \sum_{l=1}^{\omega-p}\binom{\omega - p}{l} = 2^{\omega - p} - 1$ $\text{(SM-59a)}$, the total symmetric decoupled metric-state count from SM Eq. 59 is:
$$
Z_+ = 2\left(\sum_{p=0}^{\omega-1}(2^{\omega-p}-1)\binom{\omega}{p} + 1\right) = 2\left(3^\omega - 2^\omega + 1\right) \tag{SM-59}
$$
For the physical condensation dimension $n = 6$ ($\omega = 3$), this evaluates to $Z_+ = 2(27 - 8 + 1) = \mathbf{40}$.

  * **Skew-Symmetric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ ($15$ potentials on $R_6$):** Electromagnetic field-strength vortices, chiral torsion, and rotational momentum fluxes.

  * **Korrelationstensor ($\korrelationstensor$, SM Eq. 52):** Symmetric cross-metric connections generating $n$-ary configurations (*Binär-*, *Ternär-*, *Quartärfelder*).
  * **Koppelungstensor ($\koppelungstensor$, SM Eq. 53):** Skew-symmetric connection & non-commuting metric commutator difference tensor.
* **Kontraktionsgesetze ($\kappa$, SM p. 185) & *Übergangskriterium* (SM §7.6, Eq. 64, p. 206):**

  \left( \frac{\chi}{\tau^{(p-2)/2}} \right) \sqrt{|g_{(p)}|} = 1 \tag{SM-64}

## §9.2.1: Fréchet Metric Bundles $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$ & Mixed-Variant Transport {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATIONS — NON-HERMITIAN METRIC BUNDLES &amp; MIXED-VARIANT TRANSPORT (SM, PP. 159–160)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Scholium 9.2 (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Non-Hermitian Metric Bundles):**
Why formalize Heim's *Kompositionsfeld* as ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ on a Fréchet manifold $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$?
1. **Unified Geometrization of Gravity & Electromagnetism:** Symmetric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+$ encodes Levi-Civita spacetime curvature (gravity), while skew-symmetric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ encodes the field-strength 2-form $F_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A_\nu - \partial_\nu A_\mu$ (electromagnetism/torsion) without ad hoc fields.
2. **Banach Fixed-Point Convergence:** $(\Gamma_b^0(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2(T^*\mathcal{M})), \|\cdot\|_{C^0_b})$ is a complete Banach space; modeling $\Phi_M = \bigcirc_{\alpha=1}^M(\kappa_\alpha\mathcal{T}_\alpha)$ as a strict contraction proves unique convergence to ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 9.3 (The Space of Metric Bundles $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$):**
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a smooth $n$-dimensional manifold with $n = 2\omega$.
1. **Non-Hermitian Metric Bundle:** $\operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M}) \subset \Gamma(\mathcal{M}, T^*\mathcal{M} \otimes T^*\mathcal{M})$ equipped with the $C_b^\infty$ Fréchet topology, where each non-degenerate metric decomposes uniquely:
   $$
   {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-, \quad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ \in \Gamma(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2(T^*\mathcal{M})), \quad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_- \in \Gamma(\mathcal{M}, \Lambda^2(T^*\mathcal{M}))
   $$
2. **Connection Affine Space:** $\operatorname{Conn}(\mathcal{M})$ is an affine space modeled on $\Omega^1(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{End}(T\mathcal{M}))$.
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Remark (Heim's Mixed-Variant Covariant Derivative & Transposition Argument, SM pp. 159–160):**
For a tensor with $\mu$ covariant and $m-\mu$ contravariant indices:
$$
A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu,k}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m} = \frac{\partial A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m}}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} - \sum_{\lambda=1}^{\mu}\begin{Bmatrix}s\\i_\lambda,k\end{Bmatrix}A_{i_1\cdots s\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{i}_m} + \sum_{\lambda=\mu+1}^{m}\begin{Bmatrix}i_\lambda\\s\;k\end{Bmatrix}A_{i_1\cdots i_\mu}^{\underline{i}_{\mu+1}\cdots\underline{s}\cdots\underline{i}_m}
$$
For a parallel-transported covariant vector, subtracting its index-transposed form yields:
$$
\frac{\partial A_i}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} - \frac{\partial A_k}{\partial x^{\underline{i}}} = A_s\left(\begin{Bmatrix}s\\i\;k\end{Bmatrix} - \begin{Bmatrix}s\\k\;i\end{Bmatrix}\right)
$$
*Epistemic Caution:* This identity contracts the skew connection with $A_s$; a nonzero skew connection requires an explicit nonvanishing-curl and nondegeneracy premise.
:::

## §9.3.1: Palatini Cross-Metric Connection Decomposition (Theorem 9.6, SM-53) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DERIVED MATHEMATICAL THEOREMS — CROSS-METRIC CONNECTION &amp; KOPPELUNGSTENSOR Q (THM. 9.6, SM EQ. 53)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 9.6 (Palatini Cross-Metric Connection Decomposition Theorem, SM Eq. 53):**
Let $\{g_{(\gamma)}\}_{\gamma=1}^\omega \subset \operatorname{Met}(\mathcal{M})$ be $\omega$ smooth non-Hermitian partial metrics on $\mathcal{M}$, and $g \coloneqq \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega g_{(\gamma)}$ their composite sum metric with right-inverse $g^{is}$ ($g_{sa}g^{ak} = \delta_s^k$). Let $[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}(\partial_k g_{(\gamma)sl} + \partial_l g_{(\gamma)ks} - \partial_s g_{(\gamma)kl})$.
1. **Exact Algebraic Decomposition (SM Eq. 53):** The composite second-kind Christoffel symbols $\Gamma_{kl}^i = \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}i\\kl\end{smallmatrix}\right\} \coloneqq g^{is}[s\,k\,l]$ decompose identically as:
   $$
   \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{smallmatrix} \right\} \;=\; \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega \left( \frac{1}{\omega}\begin{Bmatrix} i \\ k \; l \end{Bmatrix}^{(\mu)}_{(\gamma)} + \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \begin{Bmatrix} m \\ k \; l \end{Bmatrix}^{(\mu)}_{(\gamma)} \right) \tag{SM-53}
   $$
   where $\begin{Bmatrix}i\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)} \coloneqq g_{(\mu)}^{\dagger,is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)}$ is the cross-metric connection (*Korrelationstensor*) and the **Koppelungstensor** is the exact algebraic difference tensor:
   $$
   \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \;\coloneqq\; g^{is} g_{(\mu)sm} - \frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i
   $$
2. **Decoupling Criterion:** $\mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \equiv 0 \iff g_{(\mu)} = \frac{1}{\omega}g\;\;\forall \mu \in \{1,\dots,\omega\}$ (homothety alignment). Anisotropy or misalignment forces $\mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)} \ne \mathbf{0}$, generating non-linear cross-metric interactions.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 9.6 (Exact 3-Step Algebraic Factorization):**
1. *Linearity of 1st-kind symbols:* $[s\,k\,l] = \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega [s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} \implies \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}i\\kl\end{smallmatrix}\right\} = \sum_{\gamma=1}^\omega g^{is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)}$.
2. *Resolution of identity:* Using $\delta_a^s = g_{(\mu)am}g_{(\mu)}^{\dagger,ms}$, insert $\sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \delta_a^s$:
   $$
   g^{is}[s\,k\,l]_{(\gamma)} = \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega (g^{ia}g_{(\mu)am})\begin{Bmatrix}m\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)} = \sum_{\mu=1}^\omega \left(\frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i + \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i\right)\begin{Bmatrix}m\\kl\end{Bmatrix}_{(\gamma)}^{(\mu)}
   $$
3. *Homothety limit:* If $g_{(\mu)} = \frac{1}{\omega}g$, then $g^{ia}g_{(\mu)am} = \frac{1}{\omega}g^{ia}g_{am} = \frac{1}{\omega}\delta_m^i \implies \mathbf{Q}_{(\mu\gamma)m}^i \equiv 0$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §9.3.1b: Contortion Tensor $\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i$, Curvature Splitting & Ricci Density Curl {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: ALGEBRAIC CONTORTION TENSOR (DEF. 9.13), CURVATURE SPLITTING &amp; RICCI VOLUME-DENSITY CURL (LEMMA 9.7, SM-51)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 9.13 (Algebraic Contortion Tensor in Non-Hermitian Palatini Gravity):**
Let $T_{kl}^i \coloneqq \Gamma_{[kl]}^i = \frac{1}{2}(\Gamma_{kl}^i - \Gamma_{lk}^i)$ be the metric torsion tensor of the non-Hermitian connection. The **Contortion Tensor** $\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i$ is the unique linear tensor satisfying:
$$
\Gamma_{kl}^i = \left\{ \begin{smallmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{smallmatrix} \right\}_{{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+} + \mathbf{K}_{kl}^i, \qquad K_{ikl} \coloneqq g_{is} \mathbf{K}_{kl}^s = \frac{1}{2}\left( T_{ikl} + T_{lik} - T_{kli} \right)
$$
where $T_{ikl} \coloneqq g_{is}T_{kl}^s$. If the skew-symmetric metric sector vanishes (${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_- \equiv \mathbf{0} \implies T_{kl}^i \equiv 0$), then $K_{ikl} \equiv 0$, recovering the torsion-free Levi-Civita connection.
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Remark (Curvature Decomposition Under a Contortion $\Gamma = \Gamma^{(+)} + \mathbf{K}$):**
With $R^i{}_{klm} = \partial_l\Gamma^i_{km} - \partial_m\Gamma^i_{kl} + \Gamma^i_{sl}\Gamma^s_{km} - \Gamma^i_{sm}\Gamma^s_{kl}$, direct expansion yields the exact curvature splitting:
$$
R^i{}_{klm}(\Gamma) = R^{(+)i}{}_{klm} + \nabla^{(+)}_l\mathbf{K}^i{}_{km} - \nabla^{(+)}_m\mathbf{K}^i{}_{kl} + \mathbf{K}^i{}_{sl}\mathbf{K}^s{}_{km} - \mathbf{K}^i{}_{sm}\mathbf{K}^s{}_{kl}
$$
*Epistemic Note:* This is an exact differential-geometric curvature decomposition; an Einstein–Maxwell physical interpretation requires additional field equations and a justified source ansatz.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Lemma 9.7 (Determinant Curl Term in the Ricci Splitting, SM Eq. 51, p. 179):**
Let $w \coloneqq \sqrt{|\det g|}$ denote the metric volume density and $\llcorner_l w$ Heim's covariant volume-density derivative. The common $2\times 2$ operator-determinant term in the symmetric and skew Ricci components expands as a curl-like contribution:
$$
\frac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} \partial_l & \partial_k \\ \frac{1}{w}\llcorner_l & \frac{1}{w}\llcorner_k \end{vmatrix} w = \frac{1}{2}\left[ \partial_l\!\left(\frac{1}{w}\llcorner_k w\right) - \partial_k\!\left(\frac{1}{w}\llcorner_l w\right) \right] \tag{SM-51}
$$
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 9.8 (Non-Hermitian Palatini Conservation Constraint & Compatibility, SM Eq. 49):**
Let $(\mathcal{M}, {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}})$ have canonical first-second Ricci contraction ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{kl} \coloneqq R^m_{\;\;kml}$, right-inverse $g_{ia}g^{ak} = \delta_i^k$, and two-sided scalar curvature $\mathrm{R} \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}g^{kl}({}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{kl} + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{lk})$.
1. **Divergence-Free Conservation Identity (SM Eq. 49):** In the locally geodesic frame signature $(s_1=6, s_2=6)$ where $\Gamma=0$ (SM Eq. 42, p. 164), the non-Hermitian Einstein tensor $\mathbf{G} \coloneqq {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\mathrm{R}$ satisfies:
   $$
   \operatorname{div}_{\bar{g}} \left[ \llcorner_{(-)}^{(6, 6)}\!\left( {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} \mathrm{R} \right) \right] \coloneqq \operatorname{sp}\llcorner_{(-)}^{(6,6)}\!\left( {}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} \mathrm{R} \right) = \mathbf{0} \tag{SM-49}
   $$
2. **Palatini Metric-Torsion Compatibility Equations:** Varying $S[g,\Gamma] = \int_{\mathcal{M}} d^nx\sqrt{-\det g}\,g^{ik}R_{ik}(\Gamma) + \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}\sqrt{|g_\partial|}g^{ik}K_{ik}(\Gamma)d^{n-1}x$ independently with respect to $\Gamma_{kl}^i$ yields:
   $$
   \nabla_k g_{lm} - T^s_{\;\;km} g_{ls} + \frac{1}{n-1} g_{lm} T^s_{\;\;ks} - \frac{1}{n-1} g_{km} T^s_{\;\;ls} = 0
   $$
   algebraically fixing all $n^3$ connection degrees of freedom in terms of $g_{ab}$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 9.8 (Generalized Differential Bianchi Contraction):**
Under $\nabla$ with torsion $T_{kl}^i = \Gamma_{[kl]}^i$, curvature satisfies the generalized differential Bianchi identity:
$$
\nabla_{[m} R^i_{\phantom{i}|k|jl]} = T_{[mj}^s R^i_{\phantom{i}|k|sl]}
$$
Contracting $i$ with $j$ gives the contracted Bianchi identity for ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}_{kl} = R^m_{\;\;kml}$. Applying $\operatorname{sp}\llcorner_{(-)}^{(6,6)}$ eliminates symmetric divergence residuals and isolates stationary vorticity flux, yielding $\operatorname{sp}\llcorner_{(-)}^{(6,6)}({}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\mathrm{R}) = \mathbf{0}$. $\blacksquare$

## §9.3.1d: Tensor Densities, Divergence Splitting & the $(n-2)$ Theorem (SM-41, 44, 46, 46a) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: VECTOR DENSITIES (LEMMA 9.9), DIVERGENCE SPLITTING &amp; (n−2) THEOREM (THM. 9.10), KRONECKER NON-METRICITY (THM. 9.11)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Lemma 9.9 (Covariant Derivative of a Contravariant Vector Density, SM pp. 167–168):**
For a weight-$+1$ contravariant vector density $\underline{A}^{\underline{i}} \coloneqq p A^{\underline{i}}$, the positive-sign operator selector acts as:
$$
\llcorner_{(+),k}^{(1)}\underline{A}^{\underline{i}} \coloneqq \frac{\partial\underline{A}^{\underline{i}}}{\partial x^{\underline{k}}} + \underline{A}^{\underline{s}}\begin{Bmatrix}i\\sk\end{Bmatrix} - \underline{A}^{\underline{i}}\begin{Bmatrix}s\\sk\end{Bmatrix}_{+}
$$
**Lemma 9.12 (Metric Derivative, Inverse & Christoffel Trace, SM Eq. 41):**
For symmetric $g_{+ik}$ with Levi-Civita symbols $\Gamma^m_{+il}$: $\partial_l g_{+ik} = g_{+km}\Gamma^m_{+il} + g_{+im}\Gamma^m_{+kl}$, $\partial_l g_+^{ik} = -g_+^{jk}\Gamma^i_{+jl} - g_+^{ij}\Gamma^k_{+jl}$, and the determinant derivative gives $\partial_l \ln\sqrt{|g_+|} = \Gamma^k_{+kl}$ $\text{(SM-41)}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 9.10 (Metric Density Divergence and the $(n-2)$ Theorem, SM Eqs. 46 & 46a):**
Let $w \coloneqq \sqrt{|\det g|}$ and $\underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} \coloneqq w\bar{\mathbf{A}}$.
1. **Divergence Splitting (SM Eq. 46):** Isolating vector divergence from contracted skew torsion trace:
   $$
   \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(1)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} + \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(2)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} = 2 \operatorname{div}_n \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}}, \qquad \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(1)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} - \operatorname{sp} \llcorner_{(+)}^{(2)} \underline{\bar{\mathbf{A}}} = 2 \underline{A}^{\underline{k}} \begin{Bmatrix} s \\ sk \end{Bmatrix}_- \tag{SM-46}
   $$
2. **The $(n-2)$ Density Theorem (SM Eq. 46a):** Contracting $g_{ik}$ against the inverse metric density $\underline{g}^{\underline{ik}} \coloneqq w g^{\underline{ik}}$:
   $$
   g_{ik} \llcorner_{(+),l}^{(1,2)} \underline{g}^{\underline{ik}} = (n - 2) \llcorner_l w, \qquad \llcorner_l w \coloneqq \frac{\partial w}{\partial x^{\underline{l}}} - w\begin{Bmatrix}s\\sl\end{Bmatrix}_+ \tag{SM-46a}
   $$
   Vanishes identically for $n=2$, equals $2\llcorner_l w$ for $n=4$, and evaluates to $4\llcorner_l w$ in physical condensation dimension $n=6$.
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Theorem 9.11 (Non-Hermitian Non-Metricity on the Kronecker Delta, SM Eq. 44, p. 165):**
Heim's mixed-signature operator selector acts nontrivially on the unit tensor for off-diagonal signatures ($\varepsilon \ne \chi$): $\llcorner_{(\pm)}^{(\varepsilon),(\chi)}\delta_i^l \sim (1 - \delta_{\varepsilon\chi})$ $\text{(SM-44)}$, contrasting with the vanishing Levi-Civita derivative of $\delta_i^l$.
:::

## §9.3.2: DeTurck Parabolic Regularization & Sobolev $H^s$ Apex Convergence (Thm. 9.14) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: CONTRACTION DYNAMICS, DETURCK GAUGE FIXING &amp; SOBOLEV FIXED-POINT APEX CONVERGENCE (THM. 9.14, FIG. 9.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .fade-down}
**Why Naive Approaches Fail III: Ricci Flow's Diffeomorphism Degeneracy**
The unmodified Ricci-flow operator is **not strongly parabolic**: infinitesimal coordinate changes lie in the kernel of its principal symbol. Introducing the **DeTurck vector field** relative to background metric $\bar{g}$:
$$
V^k = g^{pq}\bigl(\Gamma_{pq}^k(g) - \Gamma_{pq}^k(\bar{g})\bigr)
$$
adds $\mathcal{L}_V g = \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i$, removing the principal-symbol degeneracy so $\sigma_\xi(\mathcal{T}(g))h_{ij} = \|\xi\|_g^2 h_{ij}$ becomes strictly elliptic and strongly parabolic.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 9.14 (Palatini Connection Uniqueness & Sobolev Fixed-Point Convergence):**
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be an $n$-dimensional compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and fix $\bar{g} \in \operatorname{Met}^+(\mathcal{M})$.
1. **Unique Palatini Resolution:** Under the Einstein–Kaufman transposition constraint and ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}}^{(2)} \equiv 0$, Palatini variation uniquely fixes $\Gamma_{kl}^i$ in terms of ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$ and $\mathbf{K}_{kl}^i$ (Thm. 9.8).
2. **DeTurck-Modified Cascade Operator:** Let $\mathcal{T}(g)_{ij} \coloneqq -2R_{ij}(g) + \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i$. For Sobolev index $s > \frac{n}{2} + 2$, the heat-regularized cascade operator:
   $$
   \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}} \;\coloneqq\; e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_{\bar{g}} + c_0 I)} \circ \mathcal{T} \;\colon\; H^s(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2 T^*\mathcal{M}) \longrightarrow H^s(\mathcal{M}, \operatorname{Sym}^2 T^*\mathcal{M})
   $$
   is a **strict Banach contraction** on $\mathbf{B}_{H^s}(\bar{g}, \delta)$ for $\tau_M \ge \tau_M^*$:
   $$
   \|\mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g_1) - \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g_2)\|_{H^s} \;\le\; k_M \|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s}, \qquad k_M \coloneqq C_{\text{heat}}C_{\text{geom}}(\bar{g},\delta)\frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} < 1
   $$
3. **Unique Smooth Apex Metric:** By the Banach Fixed-Point Theorem and elliptic regularity bootstrapping, $g^{(m+1)} = \mathbf{\Phi}_{\text{apex}}(g^{(m)})$ converges geometrically in $H^s$ to a unique ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in \bigcap_{k=s}^\infty H^k(\mathcal{M}) = C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §9.3.3a: Unsatisfiability of Literal SM-61 (Thm. 9.15) &amp; Rank-Filtered Explication {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: FORMAL REFUTATION OF LITERAL SM-61 (THM. 9.15) &amp; CARNAP SCHOLIUM 9.2</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 9.15 (Unsatisfiability of Literal Formula 61) &amp; Proof:**
Heim's SM Eq. 61 specifies the cascade multiplicity sequence:
$$
L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1} \quad (1 \le \omega_1 < n), \qquad L_\alpha = \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}, \qquad \omega_M = \frac{n}{2} \tag{SM-61}
$$
**Under the apex boundary condition $L_M = 1$, the literal cascade equalities of SM Eq. 61 are algebraically inconsistent for every manifold dimension $n \ge 2$.**

* **Proof:**
  1. For any integers $1 \le k < m$, the binomial coefficient satisfies the strict lower bound $\binom{m}{k} \ge m$.
  2. Applying this inductively along non-trivial intermediate stages gives $L_1 = \binom{n}{\omega_1} \ge n$ and $L_{M-1} \ge L_1 \ge n$.
  3. At the apex $\alpha = M$, achieving $L_M = \binom{L_{M-1}}{\omega_M} = 1$ with $\omega_M > 0$ uniquely forces $\omega_M = L_{M-1} \ge n$.
  4. However, SM Eq. 61 simultaneously stipulates $\omega_M = n/2 < n$ for all $n \ge 2$. Contradiction! $\blacksquare$
:::

    (hw1_pos : 1 ≤ w1) (hw1_lt : w1 < n) : ¬ (Nat.choose n w1 = n / 2) := by
  intro h_eq
  have h_ge : n ≤ Nat.choose n w1 := choose_ge_self_of_pos n w1 hw1_pos hw1_lt
  have h_half : n / 2 < n := Nat.div_lt_self (by omega) (by decide)
  omega</code></pre>
</div>

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.carnap-box}
**Carnap Scholium 9.2 (Explication of Formula 61 via Rank-Filtered Upper Bound):**
Rather than treating $L_\alpha = \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}$ as a literal equality on raw binomial combinations, the contractive projection operator $\kappa_\alpha$ filters out linearly dependent and zero-norm symmetric products. Replacing literal equality by the **effective rank bound**:
$$
L_\alpha \;\coloneqq\; \operatorname{rank}\!\left(\kappa_\alpha\!\left(\operatorname{Sym}^{\omega_\alpha}(F_{\alpha-1})\right)\right) \;\le\; \binom{L_{\alpha-1}}{\omega_\alpha}
$$
restores full mathematical consistency with $L_M = 1$ while preserving $\omega_M = n/2$!
:::

On an active $p$-dimensional sub-manifold $(\mathcal{M}_p, g_{(p)})$, the elementary cell quantum $\tau$ satisfies $\Delta V_p = \sqrt{|g_{(p)}|}\prod_{i=1}^p \Delta x^{\underline{i}} = \tau$. $$
\chi \sqrt{|g_{(p)}|} = 1, \qquad {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_{(p)} = \text{const} \quad \left(\text{or }\frac{\chi}{\tau^{(p-2)/(2p)}}\sqrt{|g_{(p)}|} = 1\text{ for }[\tau]=L^2\right) \tag{SM-64}
$$

## §10.1.2: *Metrondifferentiale* ($F\phi \equiv \nabla\phi$) & *Extremwerttheorie* {.smaller auto-animate="true"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: FIRST &amp; HIGHER METRONDIFFERENTIALS, LEIBNIZ PRODUCT &amp; DISCRETE EXTREMA (SM, PP. 211–218, EQS. 67–68b)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**First and Higher Metrondifferentials (SM Eqs. 67–68, pp. 213–215):**
* Because $\Delta x \to 0$ is physically forbidden, Heim replaces differential quotients with the backward **Metrondifferential** ($F\phi \equiv \nabla\phi$):
$$
F\phi(n) \equiv \nabla\phi(n) \coloneqq \phi(n) - \phi(n-1) \tag{SM-67}
$$
measuring change realized upon reaching state $n$ from its immediate historical predecessor $n-1$ (preserving causal arrow determinism).
* Iterating $F$ yields the $k$-th binomial expansion:
$$
F^k\phi(n) = \sum_{\gamma=0}^k (-1)^\gamma \binom{k}{\gamma} \phi(n - \gamma) \tag{SM-68}
$$
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Discrete Product Cross-Term (SM-68a) & *Metronische Extremwerttheorie* (SM-68b):**
* **Product Difference (SM-68a, p. 216):** Features a non-linear discreteness signature $-Fu(n)Fv(n)$ scaling as $(\Delta x)^2 \to 0$ in the continuum limit:
$$
F(u(n)v(n)) = u(n)Fv(n) + v(n-1)Fu(n) = u(n)Fv(n) + v(n)Fu(n) - Fu(n)Fv(n) \tag{SM-68a}
$$
* **Discrete Extrema & Inflection Nodes (*Wendepunkte*, SM-68b, p. 217):** Node $n=e$ is a discrete extremum if $F\phi(e) = 0$ (or changes sign): **maximum** if $F^2\phi(e) < 0$, **minimum** if $F^2\phi(e) > 0$, and **inflection node** $w$ if:
$$
\nabla^2\phi(w)\cdot\nabla^2\phi(w+1) < 0 \;\lor\; \big(\nabla^2\phi(w) = 0 \;\wedge\; \nabla^2\phi(w-1)\cdot\nabla^2\phi(w+1) < 0\big)
$$
:::

## §10.1.3: Das *Metronintegral* ($\mathcal{S}\phi$) & *Hauptsatz der Metronik* {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: INDEFINITE/DEFINITE METRONINTEGRAL, DOMAIN-SPLITTING &amp; SUMMATION BY PARTS (SM, PP. 217–220, EQS. 67a–71)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**The Metronintegral ($S\phi \equiv \mathcal{S}\phi$, SM §8.1.3, pp. 217–220):**
1. **Indefinite Metronintegral (SM Eq. 70, p. 219):** Primitive sequence $\Phi(n)$ satisfying $F\Phi(n) = \phi(n)$ with unit lattice step $Fn = 1$:
$$
\Phi(n) = \mathcal{S}\phi(n)\,Fn + C \iff \mathcal{S}\phi(n)\,Fn = \Phi(n) - C \tag{SM-70}
$$
**Boundary-Index Forms (SM p. 219):**
$$
\mathcal{S}_a^n \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = \Phi(n)-\Phi(a-1), \quad \mathcal{S}_n^b \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = \Phi(b)-\Phi(n-1), \quad \mathcal{S}_{n+1}^b \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = \Phi(b)-\Phi(n)
$$
Varying the lower endpoint gives $\nabla_n \mathcal{S}_{n+1}^b \phi(\gamma)\,\Delta\gamma = -\nabla\Phi(n) = -\phi(n)$.
2. **Definite Metronintegral (SM Eq. 67a, p. 214):** Telescoping over $[n_1, n_2]$:
$$
J(n_1, n_2) \coloneqq \sum_{n=n_1}^{n_2} \phi(n) \equiv \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2} \phi(n)\,\Delta n = \Phi(n_2) - \Phi(n_1 - 1) \tag{SM-67a}
$$
:::

::: {.remark-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Domain-Splitting Laws (SM Eq. 69, p. 218) & Summation by Parts (SM Eq. 71):**
$$
\mathcal{S}_{n_1}^\gamma \phi + \mathcal{S}_{\gamma+1}^{n_2} \phi = \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2} \phi, \qquad \mathcal{S}_{n_1+1}^{n_1}\phi = 0, \qquad \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_1}\phi\,\Delta n = \Phi(n_1)
$$
$$
\mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2}\phi + \mathcal{S}_{n_2}^{n_1}\phi = \mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_1}\phi + \mathcal{S}_{n_2}^{n_2}\phi \tag{SM-69}
$$
* **Discrete Summation by Parts (SM Eq. 71):** Inverting the discrete product rule yields:
$$
\mathcal{S}(u\nabla v)(n) \coloneqq \sum_{j=-\infty}^n u(j)\nabla v(j) = u(n)v(n) - \lim_{j\to-\infty} u(j)v(j) - \mathcal{S}\big((E^{-1}v)\nabla u\big)(n) \tag{SM-71}
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

## §10.1.4a: Multi-Variable Partial/Total Metrondifferentials & Euler Homogeneity (SM-73–77) {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: PARTIAL DIFFERENCES (SM-73), NEAREST-NEIGHBOR LATTICE AVERAGE (SM-74a) &amp; EULER HOMOGENEITY (SM-77)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Multi-Variable Partial & Total Metrondifferentials (SM §8.1.4, pp. 220–231):**
1. **Partial Difference Operator (SM Eq. 73, p. 221) & *Vertauschbarkeitssatz* (SM Eq. 73a):**
$$
F_k\phi(n_1,\dots,n_L) \coloneqq \phi(n_1,\dots,n_k,\dots,n_L) - \phi(n_1,\dots,n_k-1,\dots,n_L), \qquad F_k F_l\phi = F_l F_k\phi \tag{SM-73/73a}
$$
2. **Total Metrondifferential (SM Eq. 74, p. 222):**
$$
\nabla_{\mathrm{tot}}\phi(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^L \nabla_i\phi(\mathbf{n}), \qquad \nabla_i n_k = \delta_{ik} \tag{SM-74}
$$
3. **Nearest-Neighbor Lattice Theorem (SM Eq. 74a, p. 226):**
$$
L\phi(\mathbf{n}) - \nabla_{\mathrm{tot}}\phi(\mathbf{n}) = \sum_{i=1}^L \phi(\mathbf{n} - \mathbf{e}_i) \iff \frac{1}{L}\sum_{i=1}^L \phi(\mathbf{n}-\mathbf{e}_i) = \phi(\mathbf{n}) - \frac{1}{L}\nabla_{\mathrm{tot}}\phi(\mathbf{n}) \tag{SM-74a}
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up style="margin-top:6px;"}
**4. Discrete Euler Homogeneity Identity (SM Eq. 77, p. 231):**
For a homogeneous metronic polynomial of degree $h$ and unit lattice evaluations $n = \pm 1$:
$$
\pm \sum_{i=1}^L n_i\nabla_i\phi(\mathbf{n}) \;=\; (-1)^{h+1}\phi(\mathbf{n})\sum_{\gamma=0}^{h-1}\binom{h}{\gamma}(\mp 1)^\gamma \quad (n=\pm 1) \tag{SM-77}
$$
* **Upper signs ($n=+1, x=-1$):** $\sum_{\gamma=0}^{h-1}\binom{h}{\gamma}(-1)^\gamma = -(-1)^h \implies \text{RHS} = \phi(\mathbf{n})$.
* **Lower signs ($n=-1, x=+1$):** $\sum_{\gamma=0}^{h-1}\binom{h}{\gamma}(+1)^\gamma = 2^h - 1 \implies \text{RHS} = (-1)^{h+1}(2^h-1)\phi(\mathbf{n})$.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

<div class="video-container">
  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch10_Act4_Partial_Euler_Wronskian.mp4" style="max-height:220px;"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act IV: Commuting Partial Shifts F_k F_l = F_l F_k &amp; Discrete Euler Homogeneity (SM-77)</div>
</div>

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-left style="margin-top:8px;"}
**Geometric Meaning of SM-74a & SM-77:**
Equation (SM-74a) shows that the backward total difference measures the exact deviation of a lattice point from the arithmetic mean of its $L$ backward nearest neighbors—the discrete precursor to the graph Laplacian.
:::

## §10.1.4b: Transcendental Metrondifferences & Discrete Wronskian (SM-81–82, Thm. 10.2) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: TRANSCENDENTAL DIFFERENCES (SM-81) &amp; DISCRETE WRONSKIAN DETERMINANT (SM-82, THM. 10.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="54%"}

<div class="interactive-panel">
<h4 style="color:#FFA500; margin-top:0; margin-bottom:6px;">4-Tab Inspector: Transcendental Differences (SM-81) &amp; Discrete Wronskian (Thm. 10.2)</h4>

<div class="syn-tabs">
  <button class="syn-tab-btn active" onclick="showGenericTab('ch10-sm-pane', 1, 4, this)">1. Exp/Log &amp; Euler (SM-81)</button>
  <button class="syn-tab-btn" onclick="showGenericTab('ch10-sm-pane', 2, 4, this)">2. Trig &amp; Hyp Diffs</button>
  <button class="syn-tab-btn" onclick="showGenericTab('ch10-sm-pane', 3, 4, this)">3. Inverse Trig D_u</button>
  <button class="syn-tab-btn" onclick="showGenericTab('ch10-sm-pane', 4, 4, this)">4. Discrete Wronskian (Thm 10.2)</button>
</div>

::: {#ch10-sm-pane-1 .syn-tab-pane .active}
**1. Logarithmic, Exponential & Euler Identities (SM Eqs. 81–81a, pp. 246–249):**
$$
\phi\,\nabla_\phi \ln\phi = \nabla\phi, \qquad \nabla_\phi e^\phi = e^\phi\,\nabla\phi \tag{SM-81}
$$
$$
e^{\mathrm{i}\phi} = \cos\phi + \mathrm{i}\sin\phi \tag{SM-81a}
$$
:::

::: {#ch10-sm-pane-2 .syn-tab-pane}
**2. Trigonometric & Hyperbolic Finite Differences (SM pp. 246–249):**
$$
\nabla_\phi\cos\phi = -\sin\phi\,\nabla\phi, \quad \nabla_\phi\sin\phi = \cos\phi\,\nabla\phi, \quad \nabla_\phi\cosh\phi = \sinh\phi\,\nabla\phi, \quad \nabla_\phi\sinh\phi = \cosh\phi\,\nabla\phi
$$
$$
\nabla_\phi\tan\phi = \nabla\phi\big(\cos^2\phi + \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1}, \qquad \nabla_\phi\cot\phi = -\nabla\phi\big(\sin^2\phi - \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1}
$$
$$
\nabla_\phi\tanh\phi = \nabla\phi\big(\cosh^2\phi - \tfrac{1}{2}\sinh(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1}, \qquad \nabla_\phi\coth\phi = -\nabla\phi\big(\sinh^2\phi - \tfrac{1}{2}\sinh(2\phi)\nabla\phi\big)^{-1}
$$
:::

::: {#ch10-sm-pane-3 .syn-tab-pane}
**3. Inverse Trigonometric Selector Derivatives ($u=\phi$, $D_u \coloneqq \nabla_u/\nabla u$, SM pp. 246–249):**
$$
D_u\arccos u = -(1-u^2)^{-1/2}, \qquad D_u\arcsin u = (1-u^2)^{-1/2}
$$
$$
D_u\arctan u = \frac{1 + u\nabla\phi}{1 + u^2}, \qquad D_u\operatorname{arccot} u = -\frac{1 - u\nabla\phi}{1 + u^2}
$$
:::

::: {#ch10-sm-pane-4 .syn-tab-pane}
**4. Theorem 10.2 (Discrete Wronskian Determinant & Fundamental Systems, SM Eq. 82, p. 252):**
For an $N$-th order linear metronic selector difference equation:
$$
Cy(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \sum_{\gamma=0}^N p_\gamma(\mathbf{n})\nabla^\gamma y(\mathbf{n}) = Q(\mathbf{n}) \tag{SM-82}
$$
a set of $N$ solutions $y_1(\mathbf{n}),\dots,y_N(\mathbf{n})$ forms a fundamental basis iff the **discrete Wronskian determinant** never vanishes:
$$
D(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \det\!\left[\nabla^{\gamma-1} y_k(\mathbf{n})\right]_{N\times N} \ne 0 \quad \forall \mathbf{n} \in \mathbb{M}_\tau^1.
$$
:::

</div>

:::

::: {.column width="46%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Casorati–Wronskian Equivalence on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^1$ (Theorem 10.2 Proof):**
By multilinearity of the determinant and $\nabla^\gamma y_k(n) = \sum_{j=0}^\gamma (-1)^j \binom{\gamma}{j} y_k(n-j)$, column/row elimination reduces the difference Wronskian $D(n) = \det[\nabla^{\gamma-1} y_k(n)]$ identically to the **Casorati determinant**:
$$
D(n) \;=\; \det\!\left[y_k(n - \gamma + 1)\right]_{1 \le \gamma, k \le N}
$$
Therefore, $D(n) \ne 0$ for all $n \in \mathbb{M}_\tau^1$ is the exact necessary and sufficient condition for unique solvability of initial-value problems on the metronic lattice! $\blacksquare$
:::

## §10.1.5 & §10.2: Selektoren ($C_k$), Gitter-Moduln $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$ & Shift-Algebren {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM D/A: SELECTORS &amp; VECTOR CALCULUS (SM EQS. 78–80), SCHOLIUM 10.3 &amp; METRONIC LATTICE MANIFOLD (DEF. 10.4, FIG. 10.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.remark-box}
**§10.1.5 Selectors ($C_k$), Vector Operator $\bar{\delta}$ (SM-78–80) & Conceptual Bridge:**
* Oriented grid unit vectors $\bar{\mathbf{e}}_i$ define $\bar{\delta} \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \bar{\mathbf{e}}_i\nabla_i$ (SM Eqs. 78–80, pp. 223–235):
$$
\bar{\delta}\phi = \operatorname{GRAD}_n\phi, \quad \operatorname{sp}(\bar{\delta}\mathbf{A}) = \operatorname{DIV}_n\mathbf{A}, \quad \bar{\delta}\wedge\mathbf{A} = \operatorname{ROT}_n\mathbf{A} \in \Omega_d^2(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n) \tag{SM-79b}
$$
* **Conceptual Bridge:** Like zooming in on a digital image until smooth curves resolve into pixels of area $\tau$, **Discrete Exterior Calculus (DEC)** replaces derivatives with causal backward differences while preserving exact global topological conservation laws ($\operatorname{ROT}_n\operatorname{GRAD}_n \equiv \mathbf{0}$, $\operatorname{DIV}_n\operatorname{ROT}_n \equiv 0$).
:::

::: {.scholium-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Scholium 10.3 (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Discrete Lattice Modules):**
Why formalize Metronic Calculus via $\nabla_i = I - E_i^{-1}$ on $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)$?
1. **Causal Directionality:** $\nabla\phi(n) = \phi(n) - \phi(n-1)$ measures change from historical predecessor $n-1$ to $n$.
2. **Algebraic Telescoping:** $\nabla(\mathcal{S}\phi)(n) = \phi(n)$ without fractional boundary residuals.
3. **DEC Topological Nilpotency:** Cochain complexes $(\Omega_d^\bullet(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n), d_\tau)$ guarantee $d_\tau^2 \equiv 0$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 10.4 (The Metronic Lattice Manifold $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$ and Shift Operators, Fig. 10.2):**
1. **Metronic Lattice Manifold:** Orthogonal cubical mesh $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n \coloneqq \bigoplus_{i=1}^n \tau_i\mathbb{Z} = \{\sum_{i=1}^n n_i\tau_i e_i \mid n_i \in \mathbb{Z},\; \tau_i = \sqrt{\tau}\} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with Banach algebra $(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n), \|\cdot\|_\infty)$.
2. **Lattice Shift Operators:** Isometric automorphisms $(E_i\phi)(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \phi(\mathbf{n}+e_i)$ and backward shifts $E_i^{-1}$.
3. **Backward Difference Operator:** $\nabla_i \coloneqq I - E_i^{-1} \in \mathcal{B}(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n))$ with norm bound $\|\nabla_i\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \|I\|_{\mathrm{op}} + \|E_i^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}} = 2$.
:::

:::

## §10.2: Discrete Exterior Calculus (DEC) & Diskreter Hodge-Stern $*_\tau$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: PRIMAL-DUAL ORIENTATION (DEF. 10.5), DEC COCHAINS &amp; HODGE LAPLACIAN (DEF. 10.6, FIG. 10.3) &amp; LEAN 4 PROOF</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 10.5 (Primal-Dual Orientation and Discrete Hodge Stars):**
Let $K$ be a regular cubical cell complex on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$ and $K^*$ its circumcentric Voronoi dual complex. Primal $k$-cells $\sigma_k$ and dual $(n-k)$-cells $\sigma_{n-k}^*$ satisfy $\operatorname{or}(\sigma_k)\wedge\operatorname{or}(\sigma_{n-k}^*) = (-1)^s\operatorname{or}(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)$ ($s=0$ Riemannian, $s=1$ Lorentzian). The **Discrete Hodge Stars** $*_K \colon \Omega_d^k(K) \to \Omega_d^{n-k}(K^*)$ and $*_{K^*} \colon \Omega_d^{n-k}(K^*) \to \Omega_d^k(K)$ are:
$$
(*_K\omega)(\sigma_{n-k}^*) \coloneqq \frac{|\sigma_{n-k}^*|}{|\sigma_k|}\omega(\sigma_k), \qquad (*_{K^*}\theta)(\sigma_k) \coloneqq (-1)^{k(n-k)+s}\frac{|\sigma_k|}{|\sigma_{n-k}^*|}\theta(\sigma_{n-k}^*)
$$
satisfying exact involution duality: $*_{K^*}\circ *_K = (-1)^{k(n-k)+s}\operatorname{id}_{\Omega_d^k(K)}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 10.6 (Discrete Exterior Calculus on Metronic Lattices, Fig. 10.3):**
1. **Discrete $k$-Cochains:** $\Omega_d^k(K) \coloneqq \operatorname{Hom}(C_k(K), \mathbb{R})$.
2. **Cubical Coboundary $d_K \colon \Omega_d^k(K) \to \Omega_d^{k+1}(K)$:**
$$
(d_K\omega)(\square_{k+1}) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^{k+1}(-1)^i\big(\omega(\operatorname{Face}_i^+\square_{k+1}) - \omega(\operatorname{Face}_i^-\square_{k+1})\big), \quad d_K \circ d_K \equiv 0.
$$
3. **Discrete Codifferential:** $\delta_\tau \coloneqq (-1)^{n(k-1)+1+s}*_{K^*} d_{K^*} *_K$, satisfying $\delta_\tau \circ \delta_\tau \equiv 0$.
4. **Spatial Positive-Definite Hodge Laplacian:** On a 3D Cauchy slice $\Sigma_\tau \cong \mathbb{M}_\tau^3$ ($s=0$), $\Delta_\tau\phi \coloneqq \delta_\tau d_\tau\phi \ge 0$ is strictly positive semi-definite.
:::

structure Grid2 where (x : ℤ) (y : ℤ) deriving DecidableEq
def shiftX (p : Grid2) : Grid2 := ⟨p.x - 1, p.y⟩
def shiftY (p : Grid2) : Grid2 := ⟨p.x, p.y - 1⟩
def Form0 := Grid2 → ℝ
structure Form1 where (dx : Grid2 → ℝ) (dy : Grid2 → ℝ)
def Form2 := Grid2 → ℝ
def d0 (f : Form0) : Form1 := ⟨fun p => f p - f (shiftX p), fun p => f p - f (shiftY p)⟩
def d1 (A : Form1) : Form2 := fun p => (A.dy p - A.dy (shiftX p)) - (A.dx p - A.dx (shiftY p))

theorem dec_coboundary_nilpotent (f : Form0) : d1 (d0 f) = (fun _ => 0) := by
  funext p; dsimp [d1, d0, shiftX, shiftY]; ring
end Syntrometrie.DEC_Proof</code></pre>

## §10.3: Höhere Differenzen (SM-68), Monome & Stirling-Interpolation {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: HIGHER DIFFERENCE BINOMIAL EXPANSION (THM. 10.7), POWER MONOMIALS (THM. 10.8), STIRLING &amp; HONEYCOMB (FIG. 10.4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 10.7 & Proof (Higher Difference Binomial Expansion, SM Eq. 68):**
For any $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th iterated backward difference $\nabla_i^k = (I - E_i^{-1})^k$ satisfies:
$$
\nabla_i^k\phi(\mathbf{n}) = \sum_{\gamma=0}^k (-1)^\gamma \binom{k}{\gamma} E_i^{-\gamma}\phi(\mathbf{n}) = \sum_{\gamma=0}^k (-1)^\gamma \binom{k}{\gamma}\phi(n_1,\dots,n_i-\gamma,\dots,n_n) \tag{SM-68}
$$
**Proof:** Express $\nabla_i = I - E_i^{-1}$ in the Banach algebra $\mathcal{B}(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n))$. Since $I$ and $E_i^{-1}$ commute ($I \circ E_i^{-1} = E_i^{-1} \circ I$), the binomial theorem applies directly term-by-term. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 10.8 (Metronic Difference of Power Monomials, SM pp. 222–223):**
For integers $k, \gamma \ge 0$, the unit-step $k$-th backward difference of $n^\gamma$ ($0^0 = 1$) is:
$$
\nabla^k n^\gamma = \sum_{\ell=0}^k (-1)^\ell\binom{k}{\ell}(n-\ell)^\gamma = \begin{cases} \text{a polynomial of degree }\gamma - k, & k < \gamma, \\ \gamma!, & k = \gamma, \\ 0, & k > \gamma. \end{cases}
$$
:::

::: {.remark-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Remark (Stirling Expansion & Newton Interpolation) + Fig. 10.4 Honeycomb:**
With Stirling numbers of the second kind $\left\{\begin{smallmatrix}\gamma\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right\}$, $\nabla^k n^\gamma = \sum_{j=k}^\gamma \left\{\begin{smallmatrix}\gamma\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right\} j^{\underline{k}}(n-k)^{\underline{j-k}}$ and $(\nabla^k n^\gamma)_{n=0} = (-1)^{\gamma-k}k!\left\{\begin{smallmatrix}\gamma\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right\}$, yielding Newton's exact finite interpolation $f(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}(\nabla^k f)(k)$ for $n \ge 0$. **Fig. 10.4:** Triangular area quantum $\tau = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\ell_P^2$, discrete curl $\hat{s} \coloneqq \operatorname{ROT}_N\widehat{\Phi}$, spin eigenvalue $(\hat{s};\mathbf{n})_{\mathbf{n}=1} = \hat{\tau}$, and non-singular bound $r_{\min} \ge \sqrt{\tau}$.
:::

:::

## §10.3: Diskrete Leibniz-Produkt-/Quotientenregeln & Pseudokettenregel {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SCHOLIUM 10.9, PSEUDOCHAIN RULE (PROP. 10.10, THM. 10.11, SM-75) &amp; DISCRETE LEIBNIZ PROOF (THM. 10.12, SM-68a)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.scholium-box}
**Scholium 10.9 (The Discrete Leibniz Cross-Term):**
Backward differences obey $\nabla(uv) = u\nabla v + v\nabla u - (\nabla u)(\nabla v)$. The final term records the finite lattice step and vanishes in the continuum limit, making the discrete product law transparent.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proposition 10.10 & Theorem 10.11 (Metronic Coordinate Transformation & Pseudochain Rule, SM Eq. 75, p. 227):**
For a lattice function represented through intermediate variables $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_\Lambda$, Heim writes the total metronic difference as:
$$
\nabla\Phi = \sum_{k=1}^\Lambda \Phi_{(\psi_k)}\nabla\psi_k, \qquad \Phi_{(\psi_k)} \coloneqq \frac{\nabla_{(\psi_k)}\Phi}{\nabla\psi_k} \tag{SM-75}
$$
Because these are finite increments, the quotient $\Phi_{(\psi_k)}$ is direction-dependent and must be evaluated using the stated lattice difference convention; it is not automatically the classical infinitesimal chain rule.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 10.12 (Discrete Leibniz Product and Quotient Rules, SM Eq. 68a):**
For any lattice sequences $u, v \in \ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)$, $\nabla_i = I - E_i^{-1}$ satisfies:
$$
\nabla_i(uv) = (\nabla_i u)v + (E_i^{-1}u)(\nabla_i v) = (\nabla_i u)v + u(\nabla_i v) - (\nabla_i u)(\nabla_i v) \tag{SM-68a}
$$
$$
\nabla_i(uv^{-1}) = (\nabla_i u)v^{-1} - (E_i^{-1}u)v^{-1}(\nabla_i v)(E_i^{-1}v)^{-1} \quad (v(\mathbf{n}) \ne 0\;\forall\mathbf{n})
$$
Strict left-to-right ordering is mandatory when $u, v$ are non-commutative spin-rotor matrix fields ($\hat{s}$).
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.proof-box}
**Proof of Theorem 10.12 (4-Step Non-Commutative Derivation):**
1. Expand $\nabla_i(uv)(\mathbf{n}) = u(\mathbf{n})v(\mathbf{n}) - u(\mathbf{n}-e_i)v(\mathbf{n}-e_i)$.
2. Add and subtract $u(\mathbf{n}-e_i)v(\mathbf{n})$ (or $u(\mathbf{n})v(\mathbf{n}-e_i)$):
   $\nabla_i(uv) = (\nabla_i u)v + (E_i^{-1}u)(\nabla_i v) = u(\nabla_i v) + (E_i^{-1}v)(\nabla_i u)$.
3. Substitute $E_i^{-1}u = u - \nabla_i u$ to obtain $(\nabla_i u)v + u(\nabla_i v) - (\nabla_i u)(\nabla_i v)$.
4. For $v^{-1}$, $\nabla_i(v^{-1}) = v^{-1} - (E_i^{-1}v)^{-1} = -v^{-1}(\nabla_i v)(E_i^{-1}v)^{-1}$. Applying the product rule to $u\cdot v^{-1}$ yields the exact non-commutative quotient rule. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §10.3: Hauptsatz der Diskreten Analysis & Kontinuumslimit ($\tau \to 0^+$) {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DISCRETE SUMMATION (DEF. 10.13), FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM (THM. 10.14) &amp; CONTINUUM LIMIT PROOF (THM. 10.15)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 10.13 (The Discrete Summation Operator $\mathcal{S}$) & Theorem 10.14 (Fundamental Theorem of Discrete Calculus):**
* **Def. 10.13:** Anchored indefinite sum $(\mathcal{S}_{n_0}\phi)(n) \coloneqq \sum_{j=n_0}^n \phi(j)$ on $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{Z})$, $(\mathcal{S}_{-\infty}\phi)(n) \coloneqq \sum_{j=-\infty}^n \phi(j)$ on $\ell^1(\mathbb{Z})$, and definite sum $\mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2}\phi \coloneqq \sum_{j=n_1}^{n_2}\phi(j)$.
* **Thm. 10.14:** Let $\phi \in \ell^1(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\Phi \in \ell^\infty(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfy $\nabla\Phi = \phi$. Then:
  1. $\nabla(\mathcal{S}\phi)(n) = \phi(n)$ and $\mathcal{S}(\nabla\Phi)(n) = \Phi(n) - \lim_{j\to-\infty}\Phi(j)$.
  2. Telescoping definite sum:
$$
\mathcal{S}_{n_1}^{n_2}\phi = \sum_{j=n_1}^{n_2}\big(\Phi(j) - \Phi(j-1)\big) = \Phi(n_2) - \Phi(n_1 - 1) \tag{SM-67a}
$$
**Proof:** $\nabla(\mathcal{S}\phi)(n) = \sum_{j=-\infty}^n \phi(j) - \sum_{j=-\infty}^{n-1}\phi(j) = \phi(n)$; telescoping is immediate. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.remark-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Worked Example (1D Power Difference & Telescoping Sum) + Lean 4 Proof:**
For $\Phi(n) = n^2$ on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^1 = \mathbb{Z}$, $\phi(n) = \nabla(n^2) = n^2 - (n-1)^2 = 2n - 1$. Summing from $n=1$ to $N$ gives $\mathcal{S}_1^N(2n-1) = 2\frac{N(N+1)}{2} - N = N^2 = \Phi(N) - \Phi(0)$.
:::

<div class="lean-code-card fragment fade-right" style="margin-top:6px;">
<pre style="margin:0; font-size:0.68em;"><code>namespace Syntrometrie.StratumA.DEC_Telescoping -- Kernel-Checked S₂ (Appendix C)
theorem discrete_telescoping_sum (Phi : ℕ → ℝ) (n1 n2 : ℕ) (h : n1 ≤ n2) :
    (Finset.Icc n1 n2).sum (fun j => Phi (j + 1) - Phi j) = Phi (n2 + 1) - Phi n1 := by
  exact Finset.sum_Icc_sub h Phi
end Syntrometrie.StratumA.DEC_Telescoping</code></pre>
</div>

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 10.15 (Continuum Correspondence Limit Theorem):**
Let $f \in C^2(\mathbb{R})$ with bounded second derivative, and sample $\phi_\tau(n) \coloneqq f(n\tau)$ on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^1 = \tau\mathbb{Z}$.
1. **Derivative Convergence:** For any fixed $x = n\tau \in \mathbb{R}$:
$$
\lim_{\tau\to 0^+} \frac{(\nabla\phi_\tau)(n)}{\tau} = \lim_{\tau\to 0^+} \frac{f(x) - f(x-\tau)}{\tau} = f'(x), \qquad \left|\frac{\nabla\phi_\tau(n)}{\tau} - f'(x)\right| \le \frac{\tau}{2}\|f''\|_\infty.
$$
2. **Integral Convergence:** For $[a, b]$ with $a = n_1\tau, b = n_2\tau$:
$$
\lim_{\tau\to 0^+} \tau\sum_{j=n_1}^{n_2} \phi_\tau(j) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx.
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 10.15 (Taylor Integral Remainder Bound):**
By Taylor's theorem with integral remainder, $f(x-\tau) = f(x) - \tau f'(x) + \int_{x-\tau}^x (t - x + \tau)f''(t)\,dt$. Dividing by $\tau$ yields $\left|\frac{f(x)-f(x-\tau)}{\tau} - f'(x)\right| = \frac{1}{\tau}\left|\int_{x-\tau}^x (t-x+\tau)f''(t)\,dt\right| \le \frac{\tau}{2}\|f''\|_\infty \to 0$ as $\tau \to 0^+$. Part (2) is the convergence of Riemann sums to the Riemann integral. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §10.3: Metronischer Vektorkalkül & Diskreter Satz von Gauß–Stokes {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DISCRETE VECTOR OPERATORS (DEF. 10.16) &amp; DEC NULL IDENTITIES / GAUSS FLUX THEOREM (THM. 10.17, SM-79b–80, FIG. 10.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 10.16 (Discrete Vector Calculus & Laplacians on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$):**
With orthonormal lattice basis $\{\bar{\mathbf{e}}_1,\dots,\bar{\mathbf{e}}_n\}$ on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n = \bigoplus_{i=1}^n \tau_i\mathbb{Z}$:
1. **Metronic Gradient (DEC $d_\tau$):** $\operatorname{GRAD}_n\phi \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \bar{\mathbf{e}}_i \frac{\nabla_i\phi}{\tau_i}$.
2. **Metronic Divergence (DEC $\delta_\tau$):** $\operatorname{DIV}_n\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\nabla_i A_i(\mathbf{n})}{\tau_i}$.
3. **Metronic Rotor / Curl (SM Eq. 79b):**
$$
\operatorname{ROT}_n\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \sum_{1\le i < j \le n} \bar{\mathbf{e}}_{ij}\left(\frac{\nabla_i A_j(\mathbf{n}) - \nabla_j A_i(\mathbf{n})}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right) \in \Omega_d^2(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n) \tag{SM-79b}
$$
4. **Finite-Difference vs. DEC Laplacian:** $\Delta_{\mathrm{diff}}\phi(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\phi(\mathbf{n}+e_i)-2\phi(\mathbf{n})+\phi(\mathbf{n}-e_i)}{\tau_i^2}$ satisfies $\Delta_{\mathrm{DEC}}\phi \coloneqq \delta_\tau d_\tau\phi = -\Delta_{\mathrm{diff}}\phi \ge 0$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 10.17 & Proof (DEC Null Identities & Metronic Divergence Theorem, Fig. 10.6):**
1. **Exact Null Identities ($\forall n \ge 2$, SM Eq. 79c):**
$$
d_\tau(d_\tau\phi) \equiv 0 \in \Omega_d^2(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n), \qquad \delta_\tau(\delta_\tau\Omega) \equiv 0 \in \Omega_d^{n-2}(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n) \tag{SM-79c}
$$
recovering $\operatorname{ROT}_3(\operatorname{GRAD}_3\phi) \equiv \mathbf{0}$ and $\operatorname{DIV}_3(\operatorname{ROT}_3\mathbf{A}) \equiv 0$ via $\nabla_i\nabla_j = \nabla_j\nabla_i$ (SM-73a).
2. **Metronic Gauss Divergence Theorem (SM Eq. 80):** Over $\Omega = \prod_{i=1}^n [a_i, b_i]\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$:
$$
\sum_{\mathbf{n}\in\Omega}(\operatorname{DIV}_n\mathbf{A})(\mathbf{n}) = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{\tau_i}\left(\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{n}\in\Omega \\ n_i = b_i}} A_i(\mathbf{n}) - \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{n}\in\Omega \\ n_i = a_i - 1}} A_i(\mathbf{n})\right) \tag{SM-80}
$$
**Proof:** Mixed differences cancel by commutativity $\nabla_i\nabla_j = \nabla_j\nabla_i$; summing $\nabla_i A_i$ along each coordinate line telescopes interior fluxes to the upper ($b_i$) and offset lower ($a_i-1$) boundary facets. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

<div class="interactive-panel">
  <h4 style="color:#FFA500; margin-top:0; margin-bottom:6px;">Interactive Discrete Gauss Divergence Flux Conservation Lab (Thm. 10.17, SM-80)</h4>
  <p class="widget-context-note">
  <b>Context (Thm. 10.17, Fig. 10.6):</b> Adjust lattice box dimensions $[1, b_1]\times[1, b_2]$ for vector field $\mathbf{A}(n_1,n_2) = (n_1^2 n_2, n_1 n_2^2)$ to verify that the interior volume divergence sum equals the net normal flux across the boundary facets.
  </p>

  <span style="color:#4169E1;">Box Extent <i>b</i><sub>1</sub>:</span>
  <input type="range" id="ch10-gs-b1" min="2" max="6" step="1" value="4" oninput="ch10_updateGaussBoxLab()">
  <span id="ch10-gs-b1-val" style="font-family:monospace; width:48px;">[1, 4]</span>

## §10.3: Cubical FEEC, Whitney–de Rham Isomorphie & UV-Cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}}$ {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: CUBICAL FEEC (THM. 10.18), DE RHAM ISOMORPHISM (THM. 10.19, DEF. 10.20) &amp; UV DISPERSION PROOF (THM. 10.21)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 10.18 (Cubical Finite Element Exterior Calculus (FEEC) Convergence):**
On a uniform cubical mesh $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with trimmed-polynomial subcomplex $\mathcal{W}_\tau^k(K) \coloneqq \mathcal{P}_{1,\dots,1}^-\Omega^k(K)$ (Arnold et al. 2006; Boffi et al. 2013), smoothed commuting projections $\Pi_\tau^k \colon L^2\Omega^k \to \mathcal{W}_\tau^k(K)$ satisfy:
$$
d \circ \Pi_\tau^k = \Pi_\tau^{k+1} \circ d, \qquad \|\Pi_\tau^k\alpha\|_{L^2} \le C_{\mathrm{proj}}\|\alpha\|_{L^2}, \qquad \|\Pi_\tau^k\alpha - \alpha\|_{L^2} \le C_{\mathrm{approx}}\,\tau^s\|\alpha\|_{H^s} \quad (\text{or } h^s = \tau^{s/2} \text{ for linear mesh step } h = \sqrt{\tau}).
$$
* **Claim Ceiling ($c_{\mathrm{FEEC}}$):** *The cubical FEEC construction is a valid mathematical approximation theorem in $L^2$; it does not by itself prove that physical spacetime is discrete.*
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Theorem 10.19 (Metronic Cubical de Rham Cohomology Isomorphism) & Definition 10.20 ($R_\tau, W_\tau$):**
The **de Rham Integration Map** $(R_\tau\omega)(\sigma_k) \coloneqq \int_{\sigma_k}\omega$ and **Whitney Interpolation Map** $(W_\tau c)(\mathbf{x}) \coloneqq k!\sum c([v_{i_0},\dots,v_{i_k}])\sum_{j=0}^k (-1)^j \mu_{i_j} d\mu_{i_0}\wedge\dots\wedge\widehat{d\mu_{i_j}}\wedge\dots\wedge d\mu_{i_k}$ satisfy:
$$
d \circ W_\tau = W_\tau \circ d_\tau, \quad R_\tau \circ W_\tau = \operatorname{id}_{\Omega_d^k(K)} \implies H^k\big(\Omega_d^\bullet(K), d_\tau\big) \cong H_{\mathrm{dR}}^k(|\Omega|) \cong H_{\mathrm{sing}}^k(|\Omega|; \mathbb{R}).
$$
This isomorphism is **metric-independent**, preserving topological quantum numbers (Chern/magnetic flux charges) exactly on the lattice.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 10.21 & Proof (Metronic Lattice Momentum Dispersion and UV Cutoff):**
1. **Fourier Diagonalization:** $\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i\phi)(\mathbf{k}) = (1 - e^{-\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i})\widehat{\phi}(\mathbf{k})$ and $\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i^*\phi) = (e^{\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i}-1)\widehat{\phi}$.
2. **Positive DEC 0-Laplacian Dispersion ($\Delta_\tau = \sum_i \tau_i^{-2}\nabla_i^*\nabla_i$):**
$$
\lambda(\mathbf{k}) = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{\tau_i^2}(2 - 2\cos(k_i\tau_i)) = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{4}{\tau_i^2}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{k_i\tau_i}{2}\right) \ge 0.
$$
3. **UV Cutoff & Torus Spectral Gap:** On $\mathbb{Z}^4$, $\sigma(\Delta_\tau) = [0, 16/\tau] \text{ (since } \tau_i^2 = \tau\text{)}$, giving ultraviolet scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}} = 4/\sqrt{\tau}$; on a periodic $N$-torus, $\Delta E_{\min} = \frac{4}{\tau_1^2}\sin^2(\pi/N) > 0$ (whereas an intrinsic mass gap requires a mass term in $V_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ or compact holonomy). $\blacksquare$
:::

$$
\sum_{n=1}^N \nabla(uv)(n) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^N \big(u(n)\nabla v(n) + v(n-1)\nabla u(n)\big) \;=\; 0
$$
recovering exact energy, probability, and charge conservation on closed discrete manifolds without discretization drift.
3. **Discrete Exterior Derivative Nilpotency:** $d_\tau \circ d_\tau \equiv 0$ identically on all discrete cochains at finite lattice spacing $\tau > 0$, excluding unphysical magnetic monopoles and topological lattice anomalies.

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: METRONISIERUNGSVERFAHREN, SPIN ROTOR SELECTORS &amp; METRONISIERTE GEODÄSIE (SM §8.6, PP. 261–272)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

<h3 style="color:#5eead4; margin-top:0;">From Continuous *Tensorien* to Lattice *Hyperstrukturen*</h3>

* An abstract *Tensorion* is a continuous geometric blueprint; to manifest as a localized physical particle, it is mapped onto the discrete metronic lattice via the **Metronisierungsverfahren** (SM, p. 261), forming a **Metronische Hyperstruktur**.
* This realization is governed by three specialized filtering selectors:
  1. **Gitterselektor ($C_k$, SM, p. 264):** Enforces flat Euclidean coordinate discretization, mapping continuous $x_k$ into integer metron counts $n_k$ via $x_k = C_k ; n = \alpha_k \tau^{1/p} n_k$.
  2. **Hyperselektor ($\chi_k$, SM, p. 264):** Generalized coordinate selector for curved Riemannian configurations where ${}^2\bar{\gamma};n = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} \ne \text{const}$, establishing discrete geodesic mesh lines.
  3. **Spinselektoren ($\hat{s}, \hat{t}, \hat{\Phi}, {}^2\rho$, SM, pp. 265–266, Eq. 87):** Define intrinsic angular momentum and internal quantum symmetries:
$$
\hat{\mathrm{s}} = \ROT_N \widehat{\Phi} = \frac{\nabla_1 \Phi_2}{\tau_1} - \frac{\nabla_2 \Phi_1}{\tau_2} = \frac{\nabla_1 \Phi_2 - \nabla_2 \Phi_1}{\sqrt{\tau}}, \qquad (\hat{\mathrm{s}} ; \mathrm{n})_{\mathrm{n}=1} = \hat{\tau} \tag{SM-87}
$$
where $\hat{s}$ is the discrete spin rotor matrix fixing intrinsic spin $Q = 2J$ and ${}^2\rho$ is the metric selector governing spin-compatible symmetries.

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
***Metronisierte Geodäsie* (Discrete Geodesic Equation, SM Eq. 93a, p. 268):**
$$
\nabla^2 n^i + \sum_{k,l=1}^n \frac{\alpha_k\alpha_l}{\alpha_i}\nabla n^k \nabla n^l \Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}) = 0 \tag{SM-93a}
$$
replacing continuous second derivatives with the second backward difference $\nabla^2$ (SM Eq. 68) and sampling $\Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n})$ at discrete lattice nodes.
:::

## §11.1.3: *Strukturkondensation* ($\bar{N}$) & *Null-Stabilität* (${}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}} = \mathbf{0}$, SM-91, SM-96, SM-100) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: STRUKTURKONDENSATION, METRISCHER SIEBOPERATOR &amp; RESONANT GEOMETRIC SOLITON (SM §8.7, PP. 273–279)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
***Metrischer Sieboperator* ($S(\gamma)$, SM Eq. 96) & *Strukturkondensation* ($\bar{N}$, SM Eq. 91):**
* Cascade partial structures are filtered for lattice compatibility through the **metrischer Sieboperator** $S(\gamma)$ (SM Eq. 96, p. 274), evaluating partial metric projections against the Euclidean unit baseline.
* Total realized physical order is quantified by the **Strukturkondensation** (SM Eq. 91, p. 275):
$$
\bar{N} = \mathcal{S} \bar{K} \bar{\delta} n \tag{SM-91}
$$
where $\mathcal{S}$ is the discrete summation operator (Chapter 10) and $\bar{K}$ is the effective lattice kernel section, serving as a geometric proxy for particle number and localized charge density.
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .fade-right}
**The *Null-Stabilitätsbedingung* (Null Stability Condition, SM Eq. 100, p. 278):**
$$
{}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}}\!\left( \varsigma_{klm}^i, \lambda_m \begin{bmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{bmatrix} \right)_1^N = {}^4\mathbf{0} \tag{SM-100}
$$
A physical particle is a state of **perfect internal stress cancellation**: the metronized curvature compressor ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}}$ vanishes identically, fixing invariant particle mass spectra and the $N=6$ subspace with multiplicities $L_p = \binom{6}{p}$ (SM Eq. 100a):
$$
m = m_0 \left(\frac{\sqrt{\tau}}{\ell_{\text{hadron}}}\right)\frac{\binom{6}{p}}{6}\prod_{k=1}^3 \lambda_k(p, \hat{s})\cdot\Big[1 - \kappa_1 q_x^2 + \kappa_n(1-|q_x|) + \kappa_2|C| + \kappa_3\mathcal{P}(\nu)\Big] \tag{SM-100a}
$$
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Conceptual Bridge: From Abstract Curvature to Elementary Particle Masses**
Think of internal geometry as a musical instrument: a drum membrane vibrates only at discrete resonant harmonics. Raw metronic fields pass through the *Strukturkompressor* sieve; only configurations achieving absolute internal stress cancellation (${}^4\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{0}$) survive as *Tensorien*. Evaluated over compact $K_8$, particle rest mass ceases to be an empirical accident and becomes a topological eigenvalue locked into the crystal lattice of spacetime.
:::

## §11.2: Capacity Balance ($N=6$), 12D Fibration $R_{12}$ & Divisors (Assump. 11.1, Thm. 11.12) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A &amp; C: CAPACITY BALANCE POLYNOMIAL (ASSUMP. 11.1), SCHOLIUM 11.2 &amp; METRON DIVISOR RULE (THM. 11.12)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.firewall-box}
**Assumption 11.1 (Heim's Combinatorial Metric Capacity Balance for $N=6$, Stratum C):**
With $\omega = N/2$, count metric-condenser capacity $Z_\omega(N)$ and coordinate-deformation capacity $Z_k(N)$ (SM, p. 297):
$$
Z_\omega(N) \coloneqq 2\binom{\omega^2}{2} + \omega^2 = \omega^4 = \frac{N^4}{16}, \qquad Z_k(N) \coloneqq N^2 + \frac{N}{2}\binom{N}{2} = \frac{N^3 + 3N^2}{4}
$$
Equating these capacities yields:
$$
\frac{N^4}{16} = \frac{N^3 + 3N^2}{4} \iff N^4 - 4N^3 - 12N^2 = N^2(N - 6)(N + 2) = 0
$$
For $N > 0$, the **unique positive solution is $N = 6$ ($\omega = 3$)**, with multiplicities $L_p = \binom{6}{p}$ (SM-100a).
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Carnap Scholium 11.1 & Scholium 11.2 (Epistemic Demarcation & 12D Justification):**
* **Carnap 11.1:** The algebraic root-finding $N=6$ is exact (verified in Lean 4 below), while the capacity polynomials $Z_\omega, Z_k$ are recorded as a historical modeling assumption (**Stratum C**), not a pure category-theoretic theorem.
* **Scholium 11.2:** (1) Spectral quantization emerges from self-adjoint selectors on $L^2(\mathcal{M}, E)$; (2) $R_{12} \cong R_4 \times S_2 \times I_6$ partitions Minkowski kinematics ($R_4$), entelechial-aeonic organization ($S_2$), and internal gauge torus ($I_6$); (3) Spontaneous $N=6$ condensation locks particulate matter into $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 11.12 (Metron Divisor Selection Rule, SM Eqs. 65–65a):**
If the physical dimension $N = 6$ obeys the integer quantization relation $N = pM$ with $p, M \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, then the allowed metron dimensions under that relation are:
$$
p \in \Div(6) = \{1, \, 2, \, 3, \, 6\}
$$
*(Applies strictly to the metronized subspace parameter in $N=pM$; phenomenological resonance discussions also inspect $p=4,5$ across the full Boolean hypercube $2^6 - 1 = 63$).*
:::

## §11.2.1: $R_{12} \cong R_4 \times K_8$, Hilbert Space $\mathcal{H}_E$, $\Sel$ & $\mathfrak{D}_\tau$ (Defs. 11.3–11.7) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATIONS — 12D MANIFOLD R₁₂, HILBERT STATE SPACE H_E &amp; DISCRETIZATION FUNCTOR D_τ</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 11.3 (The 12-Dimensional Manifold $R_{12}$ and Boundaryless Internal Space $K_8$):**
The complete geometric arena of physical Syntrometrie is the 12D pseudo-Riemannian product fibration:
$$
R_{12} \cong R_4 \times K_8 \cong R_4 \times S^2 \times \mathbb{T}^6
$$
1. **Spacetime Sub-bundle $R_4(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$:** Signature $(+,+,+,-)$, observable physical 4-space.
2. **Internal Sub-bundle $K_8(x_5, \dots, x_{12}) \coloneqq S^2(x_5, x_6) \times \mathbb{T}^6(x_7, \dots, x_{12})$:** Compact, smooth, boundaryless ($\partial K_8 = \emptyset$); $S^2$ carries organizational variables ($\Delta k, t_{\text{aeon}}$) while $\mathbb{T}^6 \cong (T^2)^3$ carries internal gauge coordinates.
3. **Physical Condensation Sub-manifold:** $R_6 \coloneqq R_4 \times S_2$.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 11.4 (Positive-Definite Euclideanized Spectral Space $\mathcal{H}_E$):**
Let $R_{12}^E \cong R_3 \times \mathbb{R}^+ \times S_2 \times I_6$ be the Wick-rotated manifold with positive-definite metric $g_E \coloneqq \operatorname{diag}(+, \dots, +)$ and vector bundle $E \to R_{12}^E$ with fiber metric $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_E$. The **Geometric State Hilbert Space** is:
$$
\mathcal{H}_E \coloneqq L^2(R_{12}^E, E) \coloneqq \left\{ \Psi \in \Gamma(R_{12}^E, E) \;\Big|\; \|\Psi\|_{L^2}^2 \coloneqq \int_{R_{12}^E} \langle \Psi(x), \Psi(x) \rangle_E \, d\vol_{g_E} < \infty \right\}
$$
Bypassing skew-symmetric torsion guarantees self-adjoint selector operators with strictly real eigenvalues.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Definition 11.5 (Geometric Selector Operators) & Proposition 11.6 (4-Component Decomposition):**
* **Def. 11.5:** A **Geometric Selector** is a densely defined, self-adjoint linear differential operator $\Sel \colon \Dom(\Sel) \subseteq \mathcal{H}_E \to \mathcal{H}_E$ whose spectral resolution $\Sel = \int_{\sigma(\Sel)} \lambda \, dE_\lambda$ defines admissible physical states.
* **Prop. 11.6 (SM Eqs. 99a–99b, pp. 294–295):** In the metronized lattice representation, the total curvature-compression tensor decomposes into four sectors across partial structures $\alpha \in \{1, \dots, \omega\}$:
$$
{}^4\bar{\boldsymbol{\varsigma}} = \sum_{\alpha=1}^{\omega} \left( {}^4\bar{\boldsymbol{\varsigma}}(\alpha) + {}^4\bar{\mathbf{q}}(\alpha) + {}^4\bar{\mathbf{C}}(\alpha) + {}^4\bar{\mathbf{D}}(\alpha) \right) \tag{SM-99a}
$$
comprising intrinsic curvature-compression ${}^4\bar{\boldsymbol{\varsigma}}(\alpha)$, coupling ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{q}}(\alpha)$, cross-channel ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{C}}(\alpha)$, and mixed connection–coupling ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{D}}(\alpha)$.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 11.7 (Lattice Discretization Functor $\mathfrak{D}_\tau$):**
For a discrete lattice sampling $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n \subset \mathcal{M}$, the **Lattice Discretization Map** is the bounded linear projection:
$$
\mathfrak{D}_\tau \colon C_c^\infty(\mathcal{M}, E) \longrightarrow \ell^2(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n, E), \qquad (\mathfrak{D}_\tau \Psi)(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \Psi\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n n_i \tau_i e_i\right) \cdot \sqrt{\Delta V_\tau} \quad (\Delta V_\tau = \tau^{n/2})
$$
satisfying exact isometric continuum recovery $\lim_{\tau \to 0} \|\mathfrak{D}_\tau \Psi\|_{\ell^2} = \|\Psi\|_{L^2}$.
:::
