## §11.3: Discrete Real Eigenvalues on $K_8$ & Conjectural 3-Generation Index (Thm. 11.8) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DISCRETE REAL EIGENVALUE THEOREM ON K₈ (THM. 11.8) &amp; CONJECTURAL 3-GENERATION DIRAC INDEX (CARNAP 11.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 11.8 (Discrete Real Eigenvalue Theorem on $K_8 = S^2 \times \mathbb{T}^6$):**
Let $E \to K_8$ be a smooth Hermitian vector bundle over compact, boundaryless $K_8 = S^2 \times (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^6$. Assume the geometric selector operator
$$
\Sel \;\coloneqq\; \Delta_E + \mathrm{i}\,\rho\!\left(\iota_{K_8}^*\mathbf{\Omega}_{\text{int}}^{(12)}\right) \colon H^2(K_8, E) \subset L^2(K_8, E) \longrightarrow L^2(K_8, E)
$$
is (1) strongly elliptic of 2nd order on $K_8$, (2) symmetric on $C^\infty(K_8, E)$ extending to $\Sel^\dagger = \Sel$ on $H^2(K_8, E)$, with (3) pointwise self-adjoint zero-order gauge term $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{gauge}} \coloneqq \mathrm{i}\,\rho(\iota_{K_8}^*\mathbf{\Omega}_{\text{int}}^{(12)})$. Then:
1. $\sigma(\Sel) = \sigma_p(\Sel) = \{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^\infty \subset \mathbb{R}$ is purely discrete, real, with $\lim_{k\to\infty}|\lambda_k| = \infty$.
2. Eigenspaces are finite-dimensional, and normalized eigenfunctions form a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2(K_8, E)$: $\Sel(\Psi_k) = \lambda_k \Psi_k, \; \langle \Psi_j, \Psi_k \rangle_{L^2} = \delta_{jk}$.

<div class="claim-ceiling-pill"><b>Claim Ceiling ($c_{\text{SEL}}$):</b> Discrete real spectra are guaranteed mathematically conditional on self-adjointness and compactness of $K_8$.</div>
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Thm. 11.8 & Separated Product-Model Spectrum:**
Since $\partial K_8 = \emptyset$, integration by parts has no boundary term; $\Delta_E$ is self-adjoint and $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ preserves self-adjointness by Kato–Rellich. By Rellich's Compact Embedding ($H^2(K_8,E) \hookrightarrow L^2(K_8,E)$ compact) and elliptic regularity, $(\Sel - zI)^{-1}$ is compact, yielding a discrete real eigenbasis. For $A = -\Delta_{K_8} + V_0$ on $K_8 = S^2(R_S) \times \prod_{a=1}^6 S^1_{L_a}$, separated eigenfunctions $Y_\ell^{m_S}\prod L_a^{-1/2}e^{2\pi i m_a\theta_a/L_a}\otimes v_\alpha$ have exact eigenvalues:
$$
\lambda_{\ell,\mathbf{m},\alpha} = \frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{R_S^2} + \sum_{a=1}^6 \frac{4\pi^2 m_a^2}{L_a^2} + \mu_\alpha \qquad \blacksquare
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div class="interactive-panel">

## §11.3 & App. B (§B.5): Centered Staggered Lattice Geodesics & Verlet Precession {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B &amp; C: STAGGERED GEODESIC DIFFERENCE SYSTEM (DEF. 11.9), CONDENSATION (DEF. 11.10) &amp; VERLET ORBITS (DEF. B.8, PROP. B.9)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 11.9 (Centered Staggered Discrete Lattice Geodesic System, SM-93a):**
To align discrete 1-link velocities $\nabla n^k(m) = n^k(m) - n^k(m-1)$ with discrete acceleration $\nabla^2 n^i(m)$ at second-order accuracy $\mathcal{O}(\tau^2)$ on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$:
1. **Centered Cell-Average Operator $\mu \colon \ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n) \to \ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)$:**
$$
\mu n^k(m) \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}\big(n^k(m) + n^k(m-1)\big)
$$
2. **Centered Discrete Geodesic Difference Equation:**
$$
\nabla^2 n^i(m) + \sum_{k,l=1}^n \frac{\alpha_k \alpha_l}{\alpha_i}\big(\nabla n^k(m)\big)\big(\nabla n^l(m)\big)\!\left[\frac{\Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}(m)) + \Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}(m-1))}{2}\right] = 0 \tag{SM-93a}
$$
evaluating $\Gamma_{kl}^i$ at the midpoint of the step to eliminate grid-staggering phase errors.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 11.10 (Structural Condensation Functional) & Def. B.8 (Symplectic Verlet Stencil):**
* **Def. 11.10 (SM-91):** For effective lattice kernel section $\widetilde{K} \in \ell^1(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)$, total condensed structural information is $\bar{N} \coloneqq \mathcal{S}\widetilde{K} = \sum_{\mathbf{n}\in\mathbb{M}_\tau^n} \widetilde{K}(\mathbf{n}) < \infty$.
* **Def. B.8 & Alg. D.2 (Central Verlet Stencil on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^4$):** Unfolding $\nabla^2 n^i(m)$ yields the explicit area-preserving update:
$$
n^i(m+1) = 2n^i(m) - n^i(m-1) - \sum_{k,l=1}^4 \frac{\alpha_k\alpha_l}{\alpha_i}\big(n^k(m)-n^k(m-1)\big)\big(n^l(m)-n^l(m-1)\big)\Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}(m))
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proposition B.9 (Orbital Precession & Light Deflection on Discrete Lattices, Figs. B.2–B.3):**
In the Schwarzschild–Heim metric $g_{00} = -(1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r}), \; g_{rr} = (1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r})^{-1}$, numerical integration reproduces Mercury's perihelion advance $\Delta\phi = \frac{6\pi GM}{c^2 a(1-e^2)} = 42.98''/\text{century}$ with error $\mathcal{O}(\tau/r^2) < 10^{-40}$ and gravitational light bending $\delta\theta = \frac{4GM}{c^2 b} + \mathcal{O}(\tau/b^2)$, while eliminating $r\to 0$ continuum singularities via the minimum cell cutoff $r_{\min} \ge \sqrt{\tau}$.
:::

## §11.3: Geometric Mass-Ratio Theorem & 63-Channel Hyper-Lattice (Thm. 11.11, SM-100a) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: THE GEOMETRIC MASS-RATIO THEOREM (THM. 11.11) &amp; 63-CHANNEL BOOLEAN HYPERCUBE PARTITION (FIGS. 11.5–11.7)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 11.11 (The Geometric Mass-Ratio Theorem, SM Eq. 100a):**
Let $\Sel$ be a self-adjoint selector operator on $L_w^2(K_8, E)$ with discrete real point spectrum $\Spec(\Sel) = \{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$.
1. **Dimensionless Eigenvalue Ratio:** The mass ratio $\mu(p, \hat{s}) \coloneqq m(p, \hat{s}) / m_{\mathrm{ref}}$ of any particle state to a reference ground state ($e^-$ or $p$) is a **purely geometric dimensionless ratio**:
$$
\frac{m(p, \hat{s})}{m_{\mathrm{ref}}} \;=\; \frac{\binom{6}{p}}{\binom{6}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}}} \cdot \prod_{k=1}^3 \left( \frac{\lambda_k(p, \hat{s})}{\lambda_k(p_{\mathrm{ref}}, \hat{s}_{\mathrm{ref}})} \right) \cdot \frac{\mathcal{C}(q_x, C, \nu)}{\mathcal{C}(q_{x,\mathrm{ref}}, C_{\mathrm{ref}}, \nu_{\mathrm{ref}})} \tag{SM-100a}
$$
which is strictly non-circular and independent of the proton Compton wavelength $\ell_{\text{hadron}}$.
2. **Bridge Hypothesis ($\mathbf{C}$):** The absolute physical mass scale is parameterized by the effective hadronic scale $m_0^{\mathrm{eff}} \coloneqq m_0(\sqrt{\tau} / \ell_{\mathrm{hadron}}) \approx 173.92\,\mathrm{MeV}/c^2$ (single anchor calibration vs. 16 non-circular relative mass ratios).
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proof of Theorem 11.11 & Worked Example ($L_p = \binom{6}{p}$, Def. B.5):**
* **Step 1:** Vanishing of ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}}(\varsigma_{klm}^i, \lambda_m\Gamma_{kl}^i) = {}^4\mathbf{0}$ on $R_6$ restricts metric fluctuations to eigenspaces of $\Sel_k$.
* **Step 2:** Integrated volume condensation $\bar{N} = \mathcal{S}\bar{K}$ factors into combinatorial sub-tensor channel weights $L_p = \binom{6}{p}$ normalized by base channel $L_1 = \binom{6}{1} = 6$:
$$
\mathbf{L} = \left(\binom{6}{1}, \binom{6}{2}, \binom{6}{3}, \binom{6}{4}, \binom{6}{5}, \binom{6}{6}\right) = (6, \, 15, \, 20, \, 15, \, 6, \, 1), \quad \sum_{p=1}^6 \binom{6}{p} = 2^6 - 1 = \mathbf{63}
$$
* **Step 3:** Multiplying by the discrete spin-rotor eigenvalues $\prod_{k=1}^3 \lambda_k(p, \hat{s})$ yields SM-100a. $\blacksquare$
:::

**Scholium B.1 (Metron Scale Arithmetic and Physical Demarcation):**
Applying CODATA constants ($\hbar \approx 1.054571817\times 10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\cdot s}$, $G \approx 6.67430\times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{m^3 kg^{-1} s^{-2}}$, $c \approx 2.99792458\times 10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}$):
$$
\ell_P^2 \coloneqq \frac{\hbar G}{c^3} \approx 2.61223 \times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2, \qquad \tau_{\text{derived}} \coloneqq \frac{\sqrt{3}\hbar G}{4c^3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\ell_P^2 = \mathbf{1.13115 \times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2}
$$
$$
\boxed{\text{Correct Arithmetic} \neq \text{Correct Formula} \neq \text{Correct Physical Realization}}
$$
*(Note: $\tau_{\text{historical}} \approx 4.05\times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2$ in secondary literature uses an alternative normalization prefactor; this monograph sets $\tau_{\text{derived}} = 1.13115\times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2$ as its unified $\mathbf{S_2}$ baseline).*

**Definition B.2 (The Base Metronic Mass Unit $m_0$, Stratum C Bridge):**
The formal base metronic mass scale $m_0$ is the Compton mass associated with $\sqrt{\tau_{\text{derived}}}$:
$$
m_0 \coloneqq \frac{\hbar}{c\sqrt{\tau_{\text{derived}}}} = \left(\frac{4\hbar c}{\sqrt{3}G}\right)^{1/2} \approx \mathbf{3.308 \times 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{kg}} \approx \mathbf{1.855 \times 10^{19}\,\mathrm{GeV}/c^2}
$$
Physical rest masses are discrete fractional sub-multiples of $m_0$ filtered through $\Sel$.

\kappa_n &\coloneqq \mathbf{0.001378} \;\;(\text{Isospin Bias } m_n > m_p), & \kappa_2 &\coloneqq \mathbf{0.001210} \;\;(\text{Strangeness/Charm } |C|)\\

## §12.1.3–12.1.4: Kantian Aesthetics, Carnap's *Aufbau* &amp; Goodman's Critique {.smaller transition="slide"}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.carnap-box}
**Kantian Transcendental Aesthetics &amp; Heim's *Reflexive Move* (§12.1.3, Fig. 12.2):**
* Kant (*Critique of Pure Reason*, 1781) grounded space and time as pure *a priori* forms of sensible intuition. Heim radicalized this as **anthropomorphe Transzendentalästhetik** (Heim 2000): mistaking our species' sensory filtering and bivalent habits $\{0, 1\}$ for intrinsic ontology fractures continuous reality into artificial *Antagonismen* (wave vs. particle, determinism vs. qualia).
* **Reflexive Abstraktion:** Turns the analytical lens onto observation itself, replacing static $\{0,1\}$ projection with a Grothendieck sheaf topos over structured contexts $U = (P^U, D^U, K^U)$ glued along $\Hol(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P})$ where $\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) = 0$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Carnap's *Aufbau* (1928) &amp; Goodman's Critique (1951) (§12.1.4, Figs. 12.3–12.4):**
* Carnap (*Der logische Aufbau der Welt*, §§67–74) started from the *eigenpsychische Basis* of elementary experiences $e \in E$ and recollected similarity $P_s \subseteq E \times E$ (*Ähnlichkeitserinnerung*), defining **Quality Classes** via **Quasi-Analysis**:
$$
Q \coloneqq \bigcap \left\{ K \subseteq E \;\middle|\; K \text{ is a maximal } P_s\text{-similarity circle and } e_1, e_2 \in K \right\}
$$
* **Goodman's Collapse (*The Structure of Appearance*, 1951):**
  1. **Imperfect Community:** $\{e_1\text{ (Red, Rough)}, e_2\text{ (Red, Round)}, e_3\text{ (Round, Rough)}\}$ satisfy $e_i P_s e_j$ pairwise via *different* qualities; extensional set theory intersects them into a maximal clique, fabricating a **phantom quale**!
  2. **Companionship Difficulty:** A rare quality $Q_1$ co-occurring with pervasive $Q_2$ collapses extensionally into $Q_2$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Sheaf-Theoretic Resolution in the Operadic-Sheaf Model (OSM):**
Replacing set intersections with Kripke–Joyal sheaf semantics over $\Ctx$ equipped with Banach contractions $K^U \colon D^U \widehat{\otimes}_\pi P^U \to C^U$, three pairwise-similar contexts with no common property have trivial triple fiber product:
$$
e_1 \times_U e_2 \times_U e_3 \cong \mathbf{0}_{\Ctx} \implies \mathbf{y}(\mathbf{0}_{\Ctx}) \cong \mathbf{0}_{\Esyn} \implies \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)_{123} \ne 0
$$
The Čech descent defect diverges on the 2-simplex overlap, **rejecting the imperfect community** and rescuing qualia as **sheaf-theoretic descent invariants**.

## §12.1.7: Conditional Impossibility of Philosophical Zombies (Thm. 12.3) {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: FORMAL REFUTATION OF CHALMERSIAN PHILOSOPHICAL ZOMBIES (THM. 12.3 &amp; PROOF)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 12.3 (Conditional Structural Impossibility of Zombies):**
Let $\mathcal{N} = (P_U \to M_U, \mathbf{A}, \Osyn)$ be an active cognitive agent executing multi-modal inferential binding across $N \ge 2$ channels under the **Non-Abelian Binding Postulate** (disambiguation on ambiguous sensory overlaps requires $[a_i,a_j]\ne 0$). Define:
$$
\mathsf{Zombie}(\mathcal{N}) \iff \big(A\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{True}\big) \wedge \big(P\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{False} \iff \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \equiv \mathbf{0}\big)
$$
Then $\mathsf{Zombie}(\mathcal{N})$ is internally contradictory in $\Esyn$: $\llbracket \mathsf{Zombie}(\mathcal{N}) \rrbracket = \bot_\Omega$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 12.3:**
1. Assume $A\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{True}$ and $g_E = \frac{1}{2}\|\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}\|^2 = 0 \iff \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \equiv \mathbf{0}$.
2. For linearly independent channel 1-forms $a_1, a_2$ in a non-Abelian gauge algebra $\mathfrak{g} = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$, $\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \equiv \mathbf{0}$ holds iff $[a_i, a_j] \equiv 0$ ($\forall i \ne j$) and $a_{\mathrm{int}} \equiv 0$, reducing $\mathbf{A}$ to an Abelian Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h} \subset \mathfrak{g}$.
3. Then the carrier pushout $P_1 \boxplusphi P_2$ collapses to the uncoupled $\ell^1$-coproduct $P_1 \oplus_1 P_2$. On overlap $W = V_1 \times_U V_2$, $s_1|_W \ne s_2|_W \implies \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)_{12} = \delta^0(s)_{12} \ne 0 \implies \Hol(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P}) \cong \emptyset$.
4. Without a global section, $T_{\mathsf{P}}(X)$ cannot evaluate cross-color terms: $\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1}(\Osyn \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \bigotimes F_{\gamma_i}) = \{0\}$, contradicting $A\text{-Conscious}(\mathcal{N}) = \text{True}$!
$$
\boxed{\Omegaint \equiv 0 \implies [a_i, a_j] = 0 \implies \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) \ne 0 \implies \text{Inferential Breakdown}} \quad \blacksquare
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 12.4: Dialectical Concept Synthesis Theorem ($\operatorname{Aufhebung}$, §12.1.8)**
Let $A, B \le \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{asp}}(W)$ be two internal subobjects exhibiting an evaluative antagonism:
$$
\operatorname{Incomp}_{\mathcal{E}}(A, B) \;\coloneqq\; \llbracket |\ev_P(A) - \ev_P(B)| > \theta_{\mathrm{tol}} \rrbracket \;=\; \top_{\Omega(W)}
$$
Reflexive abstraction models dialectical sublation ($\operatorname{Aufhebung}$) as a functor mapping contradictory context $S_{\mathrm{mod}}(x)$ to successor context $S'_{\mathrm{mod}}(x')$ containing a synthesized composite whole $C \coloneqq \operatorname{Synthesize}(A, B)$ such that:
1. **Internal Consistency:** $\neg \exists A', B' \big(\operatorname{Part}(A', C) \wedge \operatorname{Part}(B', C) \wedge \operatorname{Incomp}_{\mathcal{E}}(A', B')\big)$.
2. **Higher-Level Generator:** $C$ acts as an initial generator for syndrome construction in $\Prop_{k+1}$, proving that cognitive conflict directly drives conceptual intelligence growth.

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 12.5: The Internal Heyting Mereological Universe $\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{asp}}$ (§12.1.9)**
Over context $U \in \Ctx$, the mereological universe is the complete Heyting subobject lattice:
$$
\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{asp}}(U) \;\coloneqq\; \Sub_{\Esyn}\!\left(\mathbf{y}(U) \times (\underline{\mathsf{Pred}}_U \sqcup \underline{\mathsf{Qual}}_U)\right)
$$
where parthood is $\operatorname{Part}(A, B) \iff A \le B$ in $\Omega(U)$. Relational coordination strength between qualifier $(d_r, v_{dr})$ and predicate $(f_q, v_{fq})$ is governed by a continuous Archimedean $t$-norm $\chi \colon [0, 1] \times [0, 1] \to [0, 1]$:
$$
\operatorname{Strength}\big((d_r, f_q), U\big) \;\coloneqq\; \chi\big(\zeta_r \cdot \sigma_{dr}(v_{dr}),\; \mathbf{z}_q \cdot \sigma_{fq}(v_{fq})\big) \;\in\; [0, 1]
$$
A pair is actively coordinated iff $\operatorname{Strength}((d_r, f_q), U) > \theta_{\mathrm{coord}}(U)$, satisfying constructive CEM axioms **MSL-M1** and **MSL-M2**.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.carnap-box}
**Why Constructive Heyting Mereology Replaces Extensional Set Union:**
* In classical Boolean mereology, incompatible local percepts $A, B$ with $|\ev_P(A) - \ev_P(B)| > \theta_{\mathrm{tol}}$ either explode deductively ($\bot$) or coexist as unintegrated vectors.
* In $\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{asp}}(U)$, the $t$-norm rule $(\chi\text{-I}_S)$ gates lower-level feature binding, while Theorem 12.4 lifts incompatible subobjects $A, B$ via *Aufhebung* to a conflict-free higher generator $C \in \Prop_{k+1}$.
* **Three Canonical $t$-Norm Regimes:**
  - **Product ($a \cdot b$):** Smooth multiplicative gain modulation across cortical columns.
  - **Łukasiewicz ($\max(0, a+b-1)$):** Strict finite-threshold coincidence detector.
  - **Gödel ($\min(a, b)$):** Canonical Heyting meet in the internal subobject lattice $\Omega(U)$.
:::

## §12.2.1: Mechanism 1 — Operadic Feature Consumption (*Episyllogismus*) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: OPERADIC EVALUATION (FIGS. 12.7–12.9) &amp; INFORMATION ERASURE THEOREM (THM. 12.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Operadic Feature Consumption via the *Episyllogismus* ($k \uparrow$, §12.2.1, Figs. 12.7–12.9):**
* Higher cortical tiers do **not** maintain an uncompressed pixel buffer of lower sensory arrays. Within the completed colored Banach operad $\Osyn$ (Ch. 2), multi-channel integration across levels is governed by:
$$
\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1} \colon \Osyn(\underbrace{\gamma,\dots,\gamma}_{m\text{ times}};\; \gamma+1) \;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi\; \left(F_\gamma \;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi \dots \widehat{\otimes}_\pi\; F_\gamma\right) \longrightarrow F_{\gamma+1}
$$
* Input activations at tier $\gamma$ (V1 Gabor orientations, spatial frequencies, motion vectors, A1 pitch bands) function strictly as **operands**, projected into the **coinvariant quotient space**:
$$
F_{\gamma+1} \;\cong\; \left(F_\gamma^{\;\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m}\right) \Big/ \overline{\operatorname{span}}\big\{u - \sigma(u) \;\big|\; \sigma \in \Sigma_m\big\} \Big/ \mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{relations}}
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.6 &amp; Proof (Operadic Information Erasure Theorem):**
Let $F_\gamma$ be an $n$-dimensional real Banach space representing a lower cortical feature map. Under $\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1}$, input coordinates $(x_1, \dots, x_m) \in (F_\gamma)^m$ are algebraically consumed into the coinvariant quotient. For any $n \ge 2$ and $m \ge 2$, the evaluation kernel satisfies:
$$
\boxed{\dim\big(\ker(\ev_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma+1})\big) \;\ge\; n^m \;-\; \binom{n + m - 1}{m} \;>\; 0}
$$
**Proof:** The evaluation morphism factors through the symmetrized coinvariant projection $\pi_{\mathrm{sym}} \colon (F_\gamma)^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi m} \twoheadrightarrow \Sym^m(F_\gamma)$, whose kernel is spanned by all non-symmetric tensor permutations. In finite dimensions, $\dim(F_\gamma^{\otimes m}) = n^m$ while $\dim(\Sym^m(F_\gamma)) = \binom{n+m-1}{m}$. For all $n \ge 2, m \ge 2$, $n^m - \binom{n+m-1}{m} > 0$. Because $\ev$ factors through $\pi_{\mathrm{sym}}$, $\ker(\pi_{\mathrm{sym}}) \subseteq \ker(\ev)$, erasing individual lower coordinates unless an explicit top-down adjoint section $\ev^*$ is applied. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §12.2.2: Mechanism 2 — Protosimplex Encapsulation &amp; The Metroplex Lift {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SUBOBJECT-MINIMAL PROTOSIMPLEX (DEF. 12.7) &amp; DIMENSION-COLLAPSE THEOREM (THM. 12.8, FIG. 12.10)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Dimensional Chunking via the Metroplex Lift ($\mathbf{M}^n \to \mathbf{M}^{n+1}$, §12.2.2, Fig. 12.10):**
* A distributed, recurrent firing pattern across $10^4$ spiking neurons in the inferior temporal (IT) cortex does not present to conscious awareness as $10^4$ coupled differential equations.
* In the slice category $T_n \coloneqq \operatorname{Met}_n(\Xsyn)/G_n$ of grade-$n$ configurations over blueprint $G_n$, stabilized attractor basins $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$ ($\dot{V} \le -\gamma V$) are encapsulated into atomic 0D objects of the higher-level Hypermetrophor ${}^{n+1}\mathbf{w}\widetilde{\mathbf{a}}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 12.7: Augmented Subobject-Minimal Protosimplex**
Let $T_n \coloneqq \operatorname{Met}_n(\Xsyn)/G_n$ and let $\Alg_{\mathcal{O}_n}^0$ be the category of augmented algebras over the base constant subalgebra $\Free_{\mathcal{O}_n}(\emptyset)$. An object $\mathcal{P} \in \Obj(T_n)$ is a **Protosimplex of Grade $n$** if it is non-trivial and contains no proper non-trivial augmented sub-algebras:
$$
\forall A \hookrightarrow \mathcal{P} \text{ in } \Alg_{\mathcal{O}_n}^0, \qquad A \;\cong\; \Free_{\mathcal{O}_n}(\emptyset) \;\;\vee\;\; A \;\cong\; \mathcal{P}
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.8 &amp; Proof (Protosimplex Dimension-Collapse Theorem):**
Let $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ be a recurrent neural circuit whose state space is a smooth Fréchet manifold $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{circuit}} = C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^k, \mathbb{R}^N)$ possessing an asymptotically stable attractor $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$. If $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ stabilizes into a Protosimplex $\mathcal{P} \in \Obj(T_n)$, then under the nerve embedding:
$$
N_{n+1} \colon \operatorname{Met}_{n+1}(\Xsyn) \longhookrightarrow \operatorname{Cat}_\infty(\Xsyn), \qquad \mathcal{P} \;\in\; \big(N_{n+1}(\mathbf{M}^{n+1})\big)_0 \;\cong\; \Obj(\mathbf{M}^{n+1})
$$
**Proof:** By Def. 12.7, $\mathcal{P}$ contains no proper non-trivial subobjects in $T_n$. In the complete Segal space $\CSeg(\Xsyn)$, the 0-th simplicial degree $X_0$ comprises the objects of the internal category (Hypermetrophor components). Because $\mathcal{P}$ is subobject-minimal, internal trajectories within $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{circuit}}$ collapse into degenerate 1-simplices $s_0(\mathcal{P}) \in X_1$, presenting $\mathcal{P}$ as a discrete 0-dimensional point token to $\operatorname{Met}_{n+1}$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.intuition-box}
**Why Complex Chords &amp; Semantic Concepts Feel Indivisible (Fig. 12.10):**
* **Lower Level $n$ ($\operatorname{Met}_n / G_n$):** Attractor basins $\mathcal{B}(T_{z,1})$ ($10^4$ spiking IT neurons) &amp; $\mathcal{B}(T_{z,2})$ ($10^4$ STG neurons) lift to **0D Atoms $\mathbf{P}_A, \mathbf{P}_B \in X_0$**.
* **Upper Level $n+1$ ($\operatorname{Met}_{n+1}(\Xsyn)$):** The workspace operates exclusively over 0D pointers linked by ${}^{n+1}\mathfrak{f}$.
:::

## §12.2.3: Mechanism 3 — Non-Abelian Commutators &amp; Hodge Qualia Bipartition {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: INTERACTION CURVATURE (THM. 12.9, FIG. 12.11) &amp; HODGE BIPARTITION OF QUALIA (THM. 12.10, FIGS. 12.12–12.13)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 12.9 &amp; Proof (Relative Interaction Curvature Decomposition, Fig. 12.11):**
Let $P_U \to M_U$ be a principal $G$-bundle over $(M_U, g_U)$ with non-Abelian $\mathfrak{g} = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$, and let $\mathbf{A} = A_0 + \sum_{k=1}^N a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}} \in \operatorname{Conn}(P_U)$ across $N \ge 2$ sensory channels. The total curvature 2-form $F_A \in \Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad} P_U)$ decomposes identically as:
$$
F_A \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^N \mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \;+\; \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}, \quad \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} \;\coloneqq\; \sum_{1 \le i < j \le N} [a_i, a_j] + D_{A_0}a_{\mathrm{int}} + \sum_{k=1}^N [a_k, a_{\mathrm{int}}] + \frac{1}{2}[a_{\mathrm{int}}, a_{\mathrm{int}}]
$$
**Proof:** Expanding $F_A = d(A_0 + a) + \frac{1}{2}[A_0 + a, A_0 + a] = F_{A_0} + D_{A_0}a + \frac{1}{2}[a,a]$ for $a = \sum_{k=1}^N a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}}$ and grouping single-channel terms under $\mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} = \frac{1}{N}F_{A_0} + D_{A_0}a_k + \frac{1}{2}[a_k,a_k]$ isolates $\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}$. Even when each individual sensory channel is internally flat ($\mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} = 0$), non-commutativity $[a_i, a_j] \ne 0$ generates non-zero interaction curvature with Frobenius intensity $g_E \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}\|\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}\|^2$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 12.10: Hodge Bipartition of Qualia Energy (Figs. 12.12–12.13)**
On a compact boundaryless context manifold $(M_U, g_U)$, the connection Laplacian $\Delta_{A_0} \coloneqq D_{A_0}D_{A_0}^* + D_{A_0}^*D_{A_0}$ yields the $L^2$-orthogonal Fredholm splitting in $L^2\Omega^2(M_U, \operatorname{ad} P_U)$:
$$
\boxed{\Omegaint \;=\; \underbrace{\Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}}}_{\in\,\operatorname{im}(\Delta_{A_0})\;\text{(Dynamic Flow)}} \;+\; \underbrace{\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}}}_{\in\,\ker(\Delta_{A_0})\;\text{(Topological Core)}} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad g_E = \frac{1}{2}\|\Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}}\|_{L^2}^2 + \frac{1}{2}\|\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2}
$$
* **Dynamic Intentional Qualia ($\Delta_{A_0}\Phi_{\mathrm{int}} = \Delta_{A_0}G_{A_0}(\Omegaint)$):** Transient focal perceptions, attention shifts, and adaptive sensory updates.
* **Topological Background Qualia ($\gamma_{\mathrm{harm}} \in H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M_U, \operatorname{ad} P_U)$):** Invariant self-presence and baseline embodiment.
:::

:::

## §13.1.1: Metric-Affine Qualia Geometry &amp; Non-Abelian Stokes–Wilson Holonomy {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: METRIC-AFFINE CURVATURE DECOMPOSITION &amp; WILSON HOLONOMY (DEF. 13.1 – THM. 13.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 13.1 (Metric-Affine Manifold Structure):**
Let $M_U$ be a cognitive context manifold equipped with generalized non-Hermitian metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = g + \omega$ (Riemannian metric $g$ + skew-symmetric torsion/vorticity 2-form $\omega$). On principal bundle $P_U \to M_U$ with connection $\mathbf{A} = A_0 + \sum a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}}$, the total curvature decomposes as:
$$
F_A \;=\; \sum_k \mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \;+\; \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.2 (Non-Abelian Stokes–Wilson Holonomy for Bound Qualia):**
Let $P_U \to M_U$ be a principal $G$-bundle over an orientable cognitive context manifold $M_U$ with connection $\mathbf{A} = A_0 + a_1 + a_2 \in \Omega^1(M_U, \mathfrak{g})$ where $a_1 \wedge a_2 \ne 0$, and let $\mathcal{C} = \partial \Sigma$ bound a compact 2-surface $\Sigma \subset M_U$:

1. **Wilson Loop Holonomy:** $\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\mathcal{C}) \coloneqq \mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A}\right) \coloneqq \lim_{N\to\infty}\prod_{k=1}^N \exp\!\left(-\mathbf{A}(\dot{\gamma}(t_k))\Delta t\right)$.
2. **Non-Abelian Stokes Theorem:** $\tr\!\left(\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\mathcal{C})\right) = \tr\!\left(\mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} F_A\right)\right) = \tr\!\left(\mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} (\mathcal{F}_1 + \mathcal{F}_2 + [a_1, a_2])\right)\right)$.
3. **Pure Quale Commutator Phase Shift ($\mathcal{F}_1 = 0, \mathcal{F}_2 = 0$):**
$$
\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\partial \Sigma) \;=\; \mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} [a_1, a_2]\right) \;\ne\; \id_G
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proof of Theorem 13.2 (Dyson Series &amp; Plaquette Commutator):**
Parallel transport $\Gamma(t) \in G$ along $\gamma \colon [0,1] \to M_U$ satisfies $\frac{d}{dt}\Gamma(t) + \mathbf{A}(\dot{\gamma}(t))\Gamma(t) = 0$ with $\Gamma(0) = \id$, solved by the Dyson path-ordered series $\Gamma(1) = \id + \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n \int_0^1 dt_1 \dots \int_0^{t_{n-1}} dt_n \, \mathbf{A}(t_1)\dots\mathbf{A}(t_n)$. Subdividing $\Sigma$ into plaquettes $\delta\sigma_{ij} = \Delta x^i \wedge \Delta x^j$, orthogonal transport commutators yield $\Gamma_{\Delta x^i}^{-1}\Gamma_{\Delta x^j}^{-1}\Gamma_{\Delta x^i}\Gamma_{\Delta x^j} = \id - F_{ij}\Delta x^i\Delta x^j + \mathcal{O}(|\Delta x|^3)$. Surface integration gives $\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\partial\Sigma) = \mathcal{P}\exp(-\iint_\Sigma (\mathcal{F}_1 + \mathcal{F}_2 + [a_1, a_2]))$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §13.1.2–13.1.3: Functorial *Zeitkorn* ($\delta t_n$) &amp; Saccadic Object Constancy {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATA B &amp; C: CHRONOMETRIC QUANTIZATION (THM. 13.3) &amp; PERCEPTUAL OBJECT CONSTANCY (THM. 13.4, FIG. 13.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.3 (Functorial Chronometric Quantization — *Zeitkorn* $\delta t_n$):**
Let $\mathbb{T} \coloneqq \mathbb{N}_0$ act on the sheaf category $\Sh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{syn}}, \mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}})$ by pushout endofunctor iteration $\rho(n) \coloneqq (YF_{\mathrm{model}})^n$:
$$
\mathfrak{f}_n \in \Sh \;\xrightarrow{\;YF_{\mathrm{model}}\;}\; \mathfrak{f}_{n+1} = YF(\mathfrak{f}_n), \qquad \delta t_n \;\coloneqq\; \tau(n+1) - \tau(n) > 0
$$
Subjective conscious duration is not a passive background continuum, but the discrete difference metric between functorial pushout updates (e.g., visual alpha gating at $\sim 10\,\text{Hz}$ and gamma binding cycles at $\sim 40\,\text{Hz}$, $\delta t_n \approx 25\,\text{ms}$).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.4 (Perceptual Object Constancy Theorem, Fig. 13.2):**
Let $\mathcal{C} = (B_1 \xrightarrow{\alpha_1} B_2 \xrightarrow{\alpha_2} \dots \xrightarrow{\alpha_Z} B_1)$ be a closed exploratory sensorimotor loop (e.g., ocular saccades or manual palpation). A perceptual feature $\mathbf{a} \in P^{B_1}$ represents an objective invariant entity iff its transport holonomy in the total fibration $\pi \colon \int_{\Ctx} \mathbf{Syn} \to \Ctx$ is an isometric identity:
$$
\Hol_{\mathbf{Syn}}(\mathcal{C})(\mathbf{a}) = \mathbf{a} \;\iff\; \oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{0}
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div class="video-container">
  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch13_Act2_Zeitkorn_Object_Constancy.mp4" style="max-height:215px;"></video>

</div>

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-left style="margin-top:8px;"}
**Why the World Does Not Spin When Your Eyes Move (Theorem 13.4):**
During a rapid ocular saccade $B_1 \xrightarrow{\alpha_1} B_2 \xrightarrow{\alpha_2} B_3 \xrightarrow{\alpha_3} B_1$, retinal coordinates shift violently, but corollary discharge (efference copy) supplies the exact compensatory connection 1-form $\mathbf{A}$ along $\mathcal{C}$ so that $\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{0}$. External object motion violates $\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{0}$, cleanly separating self-generated retinal slip from external physical movement.
:::

## §13.1.4: Intersubjective Faithfulness, Affinity Interfaces &amp; Theory of Mind {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATA B &amp; C: TWO-SIDED NON-DEGENERATE AFFINITY INTERFACES &amp; INTERSUBJECTIVE FAITHFULNESS (THM. 13.5)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.5 (Intersubjective Faithfulness &amp; Theory of Mind):**
Let $\mathcal{E}_A, \mathcal{E}_B$ be independent autopsychological toposes representing distinct observers mediated by a stabilized affinity interface $\beta^\infty \in \prod \Bil_{\le 1}(F_\gamma^A, F_0^B; \mathbb{R})$. Mutual intersubjective understanding is faithful and non-solipsistic iff the induced linear operators:
$$
T_\beta \colon F_0^A \longrightarrow (F_0^B)^*, \qquad S_\beta \colon F_0^B \longrightarrow (F_0^A)^*
$$
are strictly **two-sided non-degenerate**:
$$
\ker(T_\beta) = \{0\} \quad \text{and} \quad \ker(S_\beta) = \{0\}
$$
guaranteeing an injective, lossless embedding of subjective context frames without requiring identical physical substrate states.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Structural Resolution of Philosophical Solipsism:**
* Suppose observer $A$'s internal quale carrier $F_0^A$ has a non-trivial radical $\ker(T_\beta) \ne \{0\}$. Any internal state difference $v_1 - v_2 \in \ker(T_\beta)$ induces zero bilinear coupling $\beta^\infty(v_1 - v_2, w) = 0$ for all $w \in F_0^B$, rendering that aspect of $A$'s experience permanently incommunicable to $B$.
* Conversely, when $\ker(T_\beta) = \{0\}$ and $\ker(S_\beta) = \{0\}$, the curried transpose embeds $F_0^A \hookrightarrow (F_0^B)^*$ isomorphically onto its image: relational structure is faithfully transmitted across distinct biological or synthetic brains!
:::

**Theorem 13.6 (BRST Redundancy Elimination &amp; Grothendieck Fibration):**

1. **BRST Ghost-Number-Zero Cohomology:** The BRST differential $s_{\mathrm{BRST}}$ on the graded context configuration algebra $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}}$ satisfies exact nilpotency $s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 \equiv 0$. The true, observer-invariant phenomenal state space is the ghost-number-zero cohomology:
$$
\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{phenom}} \;\coloneqq\; H^0_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}}) \;=\; \frac{\ker s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=0}}{\operatorname{im} s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=-1}}
$$
which quotients out all arbitrary coordinate framing redundancies.
2. **Grothendieck Fibration:** The canonical projection $\pi \colon \int_{\Ctx}\mathbf{Syn} \to \Ctx$ from the total category of parameterized Syntrix algebras over parameter manifolds $M_U$ is a **Grothendieck Fibration**, ensuring every context transition $h \colon V \to U$ admits a universal Cartesian pullback lift $h^*(\underline{\mathbf{S}})$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Why Phenomenology Requires Gauge Cohomology ($s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 = 0$):**
* Local cortical micro-columns constantly rotate their internal coordinate gauges without altering subjective perception (drift in single-neuron tuning curves despite stable population coding).
* Passing to $H^0_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}})$ mathematically eliminates unphysical gauge-ghost degrees of freedom ($\operatorname{im} s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=-1}$) while retaining physical gauge-invariant observables ($\ker s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=0}$).

## §13.2.1: Telecentric Morse Separatrices &amp; DeTurck Parabolic Smoothing {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A &amp; B: LYAPUNOV STABILITY &amp; DETURCK SOBOLEV CONTRACTION PROOF (THM. 13.9 – THM. 13.10)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.9 (Morse Separatrices &amp; Televariant Lyapunov Stability):**
On complete Riemannian manifold $(\MAR, \gAR)$, the *Extinktionsdiskriminante* $\Dext \coloneqq \partial\mathcal{B}(T_z) = \bigcup_{j=1}^M W^s(p_j)$ is an invariant codimension-1 stable manifold of index-1 hyperbolic saddles separating the televariant attractor basin $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$ from dysvariant collapse into $\nullsyntrix$. Within $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$, the Lyapunov potential $V(x) \coloneqq \Psi(x) - \Psi(T_z)$ satisfies exponential dissipation $V(\Phi_t(x_0)) \le V(x_0)e^{-2\gamma t}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.10 (DeTurck Parabolic Smoothing &amp; Sobolev Fixed-Point Contraction):**
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold ($\partial\mathcal{M}=\emptyset$). Define the non-linear Ricci-like operator:
$$
\mathcal{T}(g)_{ij} \;\coloneqq\; -2R_{ij}(g) + \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i, \qquad V^k \coloneqq g^{pq}\!\left(\Gamma_{pq}^k(g) - \widetilde{\Gamma}_{pq}^k\right)
$$
For Sobolev index $s > \frac{n}{2} + 2$, the heat-smoothed cascade operator $\mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}} \coloneqq e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_{g_0} + c_0 I)} \circ \mathcal{T}$ is a **strict contraction** on $\mathbf{B}_{H^s}(g_0, \delta) \subset H^s(\mathcal{M}, \Sym^2(T^*\mathcal{M}))$:
$$
\|\mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g_1) - \mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g_2)\|_{H^s} \;\le\; k_M \|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s} \quad (k_M < 1)
$$
converging uniquely to a smooth stationary apex metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Four-Step Proof of Theorem 13.10:**

1. **Strong Ellipticity:** The DeTurck term kills diffeomorphism gauge degeneracy; principal symbol $\sigma_\xi(\mathcal{T}(g))h_{ij} = g^{ab}\xi_a\xi_b h_{ij} = \|\xi\|_g^2 h_{ij}$ maps $H^s(\mathcal{M}) \to H^{s-2}(\mathcal{M})$.
2. **Banach Algebra Lipschitz Bound:** Since $s > n/2 + 2$, $H^s(\mathcal{M}) \hookrightarrow C^2(\mathcal{M})$ is a Banach algebra, giving $\|\mathcal{T}(g_1) - \mathcal{T}(g_2)\|_{H^{s-2}} \le C_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)\|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s}$.
3. **Parabolic Smoothing:** $\|e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_{g_0} + c_0 I)}\|_{\mathcal{B}(H^{s-2}, H^s)} \le C_{\mathrm{heat}} \frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} \implies k_M \coloneqq C_{\mathrm{heat}}C_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)\frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} < 1$ for large $\tau_M$.
4. **Banach Fixed Point &amp; Bootstrapping:** $g^{(n+1)} = \mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g^{(n)}) \to {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$ by elliptic regularity. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §13.2.2: Universal Coalgebraic Dynamics &amp; Postnikov Truncation Towers {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: TERMINAL COALGEBRAS, TELEZENTRALENRELATIVITÄT &amp; POSTNIKOV TOWERS (THM. 13.11 – DEF. 13.12)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.11 (Universal Coalgebraic Dynamics &amp; *Telezentralenrelativität*):**
The basepoint-preserving trajectory functor $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}(M) \coloneqq (M \times C^\infty([0, \epsilon], M))_{\operatorname{ev}_0 = \operatorname{pr}_1} \amalg \mathbf{1}$ possesses a final coalgebra $(\nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}, \zeta)$ equipped with the Lambek isomorphism:
$$
\zeta \colon \nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}} \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}(\nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}), \qquad \exists! \; !_\alpha \colon (S, \alpha) \longrightarrow (\nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}, \zeta)
$$
Because the *Transzendenzsynkolator* $\Gamma_m \dashv U_{m+1}$ between scale strata $C(m) \to C(m+1)$ is a **left adjoint**, it preserves colimits rather than terminal limits:
$$
\Gamma_m(\nu\mathcal{T}_m) \;\not\cong\; \nu\mathcal{T}_{m+1}
$$
proving the mathematical relativity of telecentric attractors across hierarchical scales.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 13.12 (Postnikov $m$-Truncation Functors in $\Xsyn$):**
In the ambient higher $(\infty, 1)$-topos $\Xsyn \coloneqq \Sh_\infty(\Ctx, \Jsyn)$, structural abstraction and sensory noise filtering are governed by the **Postnikov $m$-Truncation Functor** $\tau_{\le m} \colon \Xsyn \to \Xsyn^{\le m}$, left adjoint to the inclusion $\iota_m \colon \Xsyn^{\le m} \hookrightarrow \Xsyn$:
$$
\tau_{\le m} \;\dashv\; \iota_m \implies \Map_{\Xsyn}(\tau_{\le m} X, \, Y) \;\simeq\; \Map_{\Xsyn}(X, \, Y) \quad \forall Y \in \Xsyn^{\le m}
$$

* **$\tau_{\le 0}$ (0-Truncation):** Extracts discrete conceptual objects ($\pi_0$).
* **$\tau_{\le 1}$ (1-Truncation):** Preserves fundamental groupoid relational rules ($\pi_1$).
* **Noise Erasure ($k > 1$):** Filters out microscopic thermal/synaptic fluctuations ($\pi_k = 0$ for $k > 1$).

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.13 (Phenomenal Dimensionality Condensation Theorem):**
Let a multi-tier metric cascade condense on an $N$-dimensional manifold. Equating the total metric condenser capacity $Z_\omega(N) \coloneqq \omega^4 = N^4/16$ with the coordinate deformation capacity $Z_k(N) \coloneqq N^2 + \frac{N}{2}\binom{N}{2} = (N^3 + 3N^2)/4$ yields the characteristic polynomial:
$$
Z_\omega(N) = Z_k(N) \;\iff\; N^4 - 4N^3 - 12N^2 \;=\; N^2(N - 6)(N + 2) \;=\; 0
$$
Its unique positive nonzero root **$N = 6$** proves that stable perceptual consciousness condenses onto the 6D manifold **$R_6 \coloneqq R_4 \times S_2$**:

* **Spatio-Temporal Sector ($R_4$):** $x_1, x_2, x_3$ (3D sensory receptive geometry) + $x_4$ (1D functorial *Zeitkorn* flow $\delta t_n$).
* **Entelechial-Aeonic Affective Sector ($S_2$):** $x_5$ (*Entelechy*: qualitative valence/order, $\mathcal{L}_{X_5}\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{therm}} \le -\gamma V < 0$) + $x_6$ (*Aeonics*: intentional arousal / teleological timeline).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.14 (Affective Hermetry Decomposition &amp; Divergence Conservation):**
On $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$, the non-Hermitian metric tensor ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ has 36 real components partitioned into:
$$
36 \;=\; \underbrace{21}_{\text{Symmetric } {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+} \;+\; \underbrace{15}_{\text{Skew-Symmetric } {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-}
$$
Symmetric components encode spatial extension and mesobaric homeostatic baselines; skew components encode attentional vorticity ($F_{\mu\nu}$ on $R_4$), approach-avoidance bias ($R_4 \times S_2$), and intentional agency ($[\partial_5, \partial_6]$ on $S_2$). The modified Einstein–Heim tensor satisfies:
$$
\operatorname{div}_{\bar{g}}\!\left[\Gamma_{(-)}^{(6,6)}\!\left({}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\mathrm{R}\right)\right] \;=\; \mathbf{0}
$$

## §13.3.3–13.3.4: Isocline Foliations $\mathfrak{f}_A$, Morse–Bott Centers &amp; Seeley Nuclearity {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: MORSE–BOTT CRITICAL SUBMANIFOLDS (DEF. 13.15) &amp; SEELEY NUCLEAR FRÉCHET TENSORS (THM. 13.16)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 13.15 (Isocline Submersion Foliation $\mathfrak{f}_A$ &amp; Morse–Bott Centers):**
Let ${}^m\bar{A} \colon R_m \to \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \le m$) be a smooth cognitive field. On the regular locus $R_m^{\mathrm{reg}} \coloneqq \{y \in R_m \mid \rk(d({}^m\bar{A})_y) = d\}$, the level sets $\Sigma_c \coloneqq ({}^m\bar{A})^{-1}(c) \cap R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}$ form a smooth **regular foliation $\mathfrak{f}_A$ of codimension $d$** (perceptual contour maps). Under Morse–Bott regularity, the critical locus of the intensity potential $\Phi(A) = \|A\|_{g_m}^2$ decomposes into disjoint smooth critical submanifolds:
$$
\Crit(\Phi \circ A) \;=\; \bigsqcup_\alpha Z_\alpha, \qquad \dim Z_\alpha = d_\alpha \le m
$$
where the Hessian $\nabla^2(\Phi \circ A)|_{N Z_\alpha}$ is non-degenerate on the normal bundle $N Z_\alpha$, forming stable focal attention centers.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.16 (Seeley Super-Exponential Extension &amp; Nuclear Tensor Isomorphism):**
The Seeley extension operator $\mathcal{E}^{(n)} \colon \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n) \to \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with regularized $q$-Pochhammer coefficients ($q = 1/2$) converges uniformly on orthant corners, establishing that $\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)$ is a **nuclear Fréchet space**:
$$
\mathscr{S}\!\left((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m\right) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{i=1}^{m,\pi} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{i=1}^{m,\varepsilon} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})
$$
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-up style="margin-top:8px;"}
**Why Nuclearity ($\widehat{\bigotimes}_\pi \cong \widehat{\bigotimes}_\varepsilon$) Matters for Multi-Modal Binding:**
Because biological firing rates are strictly non-negative ($x_i \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$), sensory fields live on orthant manifolds with corners $(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m$. Theorem 13.16 guarantees that the projective ($\pi$) and injective ($\varepsilon$) topological tensor products coincide canonically, eliminating ambiguity between joint multi-channel distributions and continuous operator kernels!
:::

:::

## §13.3.5: Spectral Geometry of Selector Operators on Compact Fiber $K_8$ {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: HILBERT STATE SPACE ON K_8 = S² × T⁶ (DEF. 13.17) &amp; DISCRETE SPECTRAL HARMONICS (THM. 13.18)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 13.17 (Hilbert State Space $\mathcal{H}_E$ on Compact Fiber $K_8$):**
Let $P \to M$ be a fiber bundle with compact 8D smooth boundaryless fiber:
$$
K_8 \;\coloneqq\; S^2 \times \mathbb{T}^6, \qquad \partial K_8 = \emptyset
$$
and let $E \to K_8$ be a Hermitian vector bundle. The **Hilbert State Space** is $\mathcal{H}_E \coloneqq L^2(K_8, E)$ equipped with the positive-definite Riemannian volume measure $d\mu_{K_8}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.18 (Discrete Spectral Harmonics Theorem on $K_8$):**
The strongly elliptic self-adjoint selector operator:
$$
\operatorname{Sel} \;\coloneqq\; \Delta_E + \mathrm{i}\rho\!\left(\iota_{K_8}^*\Omegaint\right) \;\colon\; H^2(K_8, E) \subset \mathcal{H}_E \longrightarrow \mathcal{H}_E
$$
has purely discrete real point spectrum $\Spec(\operatorname{Sel}) = \{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^\infty \subset \mathbb{R}$ with no finite accumulation point ($\lim_{k\to\infty}|\lambda_k| = \infty$), finite-dimensional eigenspaces, and a complete orthonormal eigenbasis:
$$
\operatorname{Sel}(\Psi_k) = \lambda_k \Psi_k, \qquad \langle\Psi_j, \Psi_k\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_E} = \delta_{jk}
$$
**Quantized cognitive attractors emerge as spectral harmonics of self-adjoint geometric selectors.**
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.proof-box}
**Proof of Theorem 13.18 (Rellich Compactness &amp; Spectral Resolution):**
1. **Self-Adjointness:** Since $\partial K_8 = \emptyset$, the connection Laplacian $\Delta_E = \nabla^*\nabla$ is essentially self-adjoint on $H^2(K_8, E)$. Because $\Omegaint$ takes values in a skew-Hermitian Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g} \subset \mathfrak{u}(N)$, multiplication by $\mathrm{i}\rho(\iota_{K_8}^*\Omegaint)$ is a bounded pointwise self-adjoint 0th-order perturbation.
2. **Compact Resolvent:** By **Rellich's Kondrachov Compactness Theorem** on the closed manifold $K_8$, the Sobolev embedding $H^2(K_8, E) \hookrightarrow L^2(K_8, E)$ is a compact operator.
3. **Discrete Eigenbasis:** Elliptic regularity implies that the resolvent $(\operatorname{Sel} - \lambda I)^{-1} \colon L^2 \to H^2 \hookrightarrow L^2$ is compact for $\lambda \notin \mathbb{R}$. The spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators with compact resolvent yields a complete orthonormal basis of smooth eigenfunctions $\{\Psi_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$ with real eigenvalues $|\lambda_k| \to \infty$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §13.3.6: Stokes–Cartan FEEC Discretization &amp; Metronic Lattice UV Cutoff {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: EXACT DE RHAM COCHAIN COMMUTATIVITY &amp; BRILLOUIN DISPERSION (THMS. 13.19 – 13.20)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.19 (Commutativity of the Stokes–Cartan Discretization Functor):**
Let $K$ be a regular cubical cell complex discretizing smooth orientable manifold $\mathcal{M}_n$ at linear mesh spacing $\sqrt{\tau} > 0$. The de Rham integration projection $(\mathcal{R}_\tau^k \omega)(\sigma_k) \coloneqq \int_{\sigma_k} \omega$ commutes strictly with the discrete coboundary $d_\tau$ in $\mathbf{Ch}_{\ge 0}(\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}})$:
$$
d_\tau \circ \mathcal{R}_\tau^k \;=\; \mathcal{R}_\tau^{k+1} \circ d, \qquad \|\Pi_\tau^k \alpha - \alpha\|_{L^2} \;\le\; C_{\mathrm{approx}}\, \tau^{s/2} \|\alpha\|_{H^s} \;\; (0 < s \le 1)
$$
**3-Step Proof:** For $(k+1)$-cell $\sigma_{k+1}$ with boundary $\partial\sigma_{k+1} = \sum_j (-1)^j \operatorname{Face}_j(\sigma_{k+1})$:
(1) $((\mathcal{R}_\tau^{k+1}\circ d)\omega)(\sigma_{k+1}) = \int_{\sigma_{k+1}} d\omega$;
(2) $((d_\tau \circ \mathcal{R}_\tau^k)\omega)(\sigma_{k+1}) = (\mathcal{R}_\tau^k\omega)(\partial\sigma_{k+1}) = \int_{\partial\sigma_{k+1}}\omega$;
(3) Classical Stokes' Theorem $\int_{\sigma_{k+1}} d\omega = \int_{\partial\sigma_{k+1}}\omega$ equates both paths. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Corollary 13.20 (Metronic Lattice Momentum Dispersion &amp; UV Cutoff):**
On the uniform discrete metronic lattice $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n = \bigoplus_{i=1}^n \tau_i\mathbb{Z}$ ($\tau_i^2 = \tau$):

1. **Fourier Diagonalization:** $\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i\phi)(\mathbf{k}) = (1 - e^{-\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i})\widehat{\phi}(\mathbf{k})$ and $\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i^*\phi) = (e^{\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i}-1)\widehat{\phi}(\mathbf{k})$.
2. **DEC 0-Laplacian Dispersion ($\Delta_\tau = \sum_i \tau_i^{-2}\nabla_i^*\nabla_i$):**
$$
\lambda(\mathbf{k}) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{2}{\tau_i^2}\!\left(1 - \cos(k_i\tau_i)\right) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{4}{\tau_i^2}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{k_i\tau_i}{2}\right) \;\ge\; 0
$$
3. **UV Cutoff &amp; Torus IR Gap:** On $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$, $\sigma(\Delta_\tau) = [0, 4n/\tau]$ gives ultraviolet cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}} = 2\sqrt{n}/\sqrt{\tau}$ ($4/\sqrt{\tau}$ for $n=4$); on a finite periodic $N$-torus ($k_i = \frac{2\pi m_i}{N\tau_i}$), the lowest non-zero mode $\mathbf{m}=(1,0,\dots,0)$ has strictly positive gap $\Delta E_{\min} = \frac{4}{\tau}\sin^2(\pi/N) > 0$.
4. **Intrinsic Mass Gap:** Requires non-vanishing mass term in $V_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ or compact holonomy. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §13.5: Topos Integrated Information $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$ vs. Classical IIT 4.0 {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATA A, B &amp; C: HOMOLOGICAL INTEGRATION INVARIANT &amp; POLYNOMIAL COMPLEXITY (DEF. 13.21 – PROP. 13.23)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Bottlenecks of Classical IIT 4.0 (Tononi) vs. Definition 13.21 ($\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$):**
Standard IIT 4.0 suffers from **(1) Combinatorial Intractability** ($\mathcal{O}(2^N)$ Minimum Information Partition search over $\mathcal{P}(V\times V)$, uncomputable for $N > 12$) and **(2) Arbitrary Probability Metrics** (extrinsic EMD/KL divergence). In Syntrometrie, for active network $\mathcal{N} = (\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P}, \mathbf{A})$ covered by $\mathcal{U} = \{V_i \to U\}_{i=1}^m$, the **Topos Integrated Information Index** is:
$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P}) \;\coloneqq\; \left\|\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}\right\|_{L^2\Omega^2} \;\cdot\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{\|\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)\|_{\check{C}^1}^2}{2\sigma_{\mathrm{tol}}^2}\right)
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.22 (Equivalence &amp; Superiority of $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$):**
$\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$ satisfies all five IIT 4.0 axioms (Existence, Intrinsicality, Information, Integration, Exclusion) while resolving combinatorial complexity:

1. **Causal Independence (Zero Integration):** Uncoupled modules $P_1 \oplus_1 P_2 \implies [a_i, a_j] \equiv 0 \implies \Omegaint \equiv \mathbf{0} \implies \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}} = 0$.
2. **Descent Consistency (Exclusion):** Contradictory overlaps $s_i|_{V_{ij}} \ne s_j|_{V_{ij}} \implies \|\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)\| \to \infty \implies \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}} \to 0$ exponentially.
3. **Polynomial Complexity:** Computing $\binom{N}{2}$ pairwise Lie brackets $[a_i, a_j]$ along active edges $E \subset V\times V$ scales as **$\mathcal{O}(|E|) \le \mathcal{O}(N^2)$** vs. $\mathcal{O}(2^N)$ MIP cuts. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proposition 13.23 (Explicit Three-Node $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Evaluation Across Regimes):**
For 3 modules with strengths $\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3$ and $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators $\|T_k\| = 1/2$, curvature $\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} = \omega_1\omega_2 T_3 dx^1\wedge dx^2 + \omega_2\omega_3 T_1 dx^2\wedge dx^3 + \omega_3\omega_1 T_2 dx^3\wedge dx^1$ yields:

* **1. Bound Triad ($\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)=0$):** $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{bound}} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\omega_1^2\omega_2^2 + \omega_2^2\omega_3^2 + \omega_3^2\omega_1^2}$.
* **2. Abelian Split:** All channels in an Abelian subalgebra $\implies \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{split}} = 0$.
* **3. Contradictory Rivalry ($\|\Def\| = \Delta v$):** $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{rivalry}} = \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{bound}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(\Delta v)^2}{2\sigma_{\mathrm{tol}}^2}\right) \to 0$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §13.6.1: The Geometry of Self-Consciousness &amp; Lawvere Fixed Points {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: CURRY–HOWARD PROOF OF THE LAWVERE EGO FIXED-POINT THEOREM (THM. 13.24)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="52%"}

<h3 style="color:#FFD700; margin-top:0;">Resolving the Homuncular Regress of *Ich-Bewusstsein*</h3>

* How does a cognitive system achieve **self-awareness** (*Ich-Bewusstsein*) without triggering an infinite homuncular regress (an observer observing an observer observing...)?
* Following F. William Lawvere's (1969) categorical diagonal theorem, self-consciousness is not a separate meta-module, but the **invariant diagonal fixed point $e^* \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$** of the internal evaluation morphism in a cartesian closed category (CCC).

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.24 (Curry–Howard Categorical Proof of the Lawvere Ego Fixed Point):**
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a cartesian closed category with terminal object $\mathbf{1}$, internal evaluation object $\Omega$, and observer internal state space $A \in \Obj(\mathcal{C})$. If an internal evaluation morphism $\Phi \colon A \times A \to \Omega$ is **point-surjective** (its curried transpose $\hat{\Phi} \colon A \to \Omega^A$ has a right section on global elements), then **every endomorphism $f \colon \Omega \to \Omega$ possesses a fixed point** $y^* \in \Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \Omega)$:
$$
f \circ y^* \;=\; y^*
$$
In particular, the self-reflective diagonal $\Delta_A \colon A \to A \times A$ induces an invariant self-representation (**Ego Token**) $e^* \in \Hom(\mathbf{1}, A)$ satisfying:
$$
\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle \;=\; f\!\left(\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle\right)
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Complete Three-Step Diagram-Chase Proof of Theorem 13.24:**

* **Step 1 (Construction of the Diagonal Functional):**
  Let $\Delta_A \coloneqq \langle \id_A, \id_A \rangle \colon A \to A \times A$ be the canonical diagonal morphism. Define the self-evaluating diagonal arrow $\delta \coloneqq \Phi \circ \Delta_A \colon A \to \Omega$. Post-composing with $f \colon \Omega \to \Omega$ yields the modified diagonal functional:
  $$
  g \;\coloneqq\; f \circ \delta \;=\; f \circ \Phi \circ \langle \id_A, \id_A \rangle \;\colon\; A \longrightarrow \Omega
  $$
* **Step 2 (Currying &amp; Surjectivity Inversion):**
  By cartesian closure, $\Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(A \times A, \Omega) \cong \Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(A, \Omega^A)$ via exponential transpose $\hat{\Phi} \colon A \to \Omega^A$. The arrow $g \colon A \to \Omega$ corresponds under adjunction to a global element $\ulcorner g \urcorner \colon \mathbf{1} \to \Omega^A$. By point-surjectivity of $\hat{\Phi}$ on global elements $\Hom(\mathbf{1}, A) \to \Hom(\mathbf{1}, \Omega^A)$, there exists a representing global element (the **Ego Token** $e^*$):
  $$
  e^* \;\colon\; \mathbf{1} \longrightarrow A \quad \text{such that} \quad \hat{\Phi} \circ e^* \;=\; \ulcorner g \urcorner
  $$
* **Step 3 (Evaluation Along the Diagonal):**
  Uncurrying $\hat{\Phi} \circ e^* = \ulcorner g \urcorner$ implies that for all generalized elements $x \colon X \to A$:
  $$
  \Phi \circ \langle e^* \circ !_X, \; x \rangle \;=\; g \circ x \;=\; f \circ \Phi \circ \langle x, x \rangle
  $$
  Instantiating $X \coloneqq \mathbf{1}$ and setting $x \coloneqq e^* \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ yields $\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle = f(\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle)$. Setting $y^* \coloneqq \Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle \colon \mathbf{1} \to \Omega$ gives $f \circ y^* = y^*$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §13.6.2: Active Inference as Sheaf Descent Optimization (Thm. 13.25) {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-c">STRATUM C: FRISTON'S ACTIVE INFERENCE AS ČECH DESCENT &amp; LYAPUNOV MINIMIZATION (THM. 13.25, FIG. 13.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.25 (Active Inference Sheaf Descent Theorem — Friston Formalized):**
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{V_i \to U\}$ be a sensory covering family in predictive processing:

1. **Prediction Errors are Čech Descent Defects:** The discrepancy between top-down generative priors ($s_{\mathrm{prior}} \in \mathbf{P}(U)$) and bottom-up sensory data ($s_{\mathrm{sens}} \in \check{C}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P})$) is the Čech 0-coboundary:
$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pred}} \;\coloneqq\; \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) \;=\; d^0(s) - d^1(s) \;\in\; \check{C}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{A})
$$
2. **Free-Energy Minimization is Lyapunov Descent:** Variational Free Energy $F$ is identical to the Lyapunov potential $V(x) \coloneqq \Psi(x) - \Psi(T_z)$ on $\MAR$:
$$
\dot{F} \le -\gamma F \;\iff\; \dot{V}(x) \le -\gamma V(x) \quad (\text{Televariant Convergence to Prior } T_z)
$$
3. **Active Motor Action as Context Morphism:** When internal synaptic weight updates cannot eliminate $\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) \ne 0$, the agent executes an active motor action (saccade, locomotion) $\alpha \colon U \to U'$ shifting physical sensors to force $\Def_{\mathcal{U}'}(s') \to 0$.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Figure 13.6: The Reflexive Self-Consciousness &amp; Active Inference Loop**
* **Top-Down Generative Prior ($U \in \Ctx$):** Representable sheaf $\mathbf{y}(U)$ projects prior expectation $s_{\mathrm{prior}} \in \mathbf{P}(U)$ onto sensory overlaps $V_{ij} = V_i \times_U V_j$.
* **Two Dual Descent Pathways to Eliminate $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pred}} = \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)$:**
  1. **Perceptual Inference (Internal Synaptic Tuning):** Gradient descent $\dot{V} \le -\gamma V$ updates internal model parameters toward telecentre $T_z$.
  2. **Active Inference (Motor Context Morphism):** Base morphism $\alpha \colon U \to U'$ re-orients sensory organs until pullback sections agree ($\Def_{\mathcal{U}'}(s') = 0$).
* **Lawvere Closure:** Closed at the base by the invariant ego-token $e^* = \operatorname{Self}$ satisfying $\Phi_{\mathrm{ego}}(e^*, x) = f(\Phi_{\mathrm{ego}}(x, x))$.
:::

<pre class="lean-code-card">lemma opNorm_comp_le_one {E F G : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G]
    (f : E →L[ℝ] F) (g : F →L[ℝ] G) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1) (hg : ‖g‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖g.comp f‖ ≤ 1 := by
  calc ‖g.comp f‖ ≤ ‖g‖ * ‖f‖ := ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le g f
    _ ≤ 1 * 1 := mul_le_mul hg hf (norm_nonneg f) zero_le_one
    _ = 1 := mul_one 1
instance : Category ContextObject where

  id U := {
    alpha_D := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.D, alpha_D_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    alpha_P := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.P, alpha_P_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    alpha_C := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.C, alpha_C_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    comm := fun _ _ =&gt; rfl, cipher_z := fun _ =&gt; rfl, cipher_zeta := fun _ =&gt; rfl
  }
  comp f g := {
    alpha_D := g.alpha_D.comp f.alpha_D
    alpha_D_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_D g.alpha_D f.alpha_D_contractive g.alpha_D_contractive
    alpha_P := g.alpha_P.comp f.alpha_P
    alpha_P_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_P g.alpha_P f.alpha_P_contractive g.alpha_P_contractive
    alpha_C := g.alpha_C.comp f.alpha_C

    cipher_z := fun p =&gt; by dsimp; rw [f.cipher_z, g.cipher_z]
    cipher_zeta := fun d =&gt; by dsimp; rw [f.cipher_zeta, g.cipher_zeta]
  }</pre>

<pre class="lean-code-card">/-- Collect constants occurring in an expression via AST fold (App. C, Module 6) -/
def constantsInExpr (e : Expr) : NameSet :=
  e.foldConsts NameSet.empty (fun n acc => acc.insert n)

partial def getTransitiveConstants (env : Environment) (root : Name) : NameSet :=
  let rec visit (curr : Name) (visited : NameSet) : NameSet :=
    if visited.contains curr then visited else
      let visited' := visited.insert curr
      match env.find? curr with
      | some info =>
          let visited1 := (constantsInExpr info.type).fold (fun acc c => visit c acc) visited'
          match info.value? with
          | some val => (constantsInExpr val).fold (fun acc c => visit c acc) visited1
          | none => visited1
      | none => visited'
  visit root NameSet.empty

def checkTransitiveFirewall (declName : Name) (tag : ProvenanceTag) : CoreM Unit := do
  let env &lt;- getEnv
  let deps := getTransitiveConstants env declName
  if tag.stratum == Stratum.StratumA || tag.stratum == Stratum.StratumB then
    if tag.type == EpistemicType.PhysicalHypothesis then
      throwError "EPISTEMIC FIREWALL BREACH: Stratum A/B declaration tagged [P]."
    for depName in deps do
      if let some depTag := provenanceMap.getState env |&gt;.find? depName then
        if depTag.type == EpistemicType.PhysicalHypothesis || depTag.stratum == Stratum.StratumD then
          throwError "EPISTEMIC FIREWALL BREACH: forbidden transitive dependency."</pre>

::: {.thm-box}
**Conjecture 1 (§15.4.1): Topos-Relative Completeness of $\LiMSL$**
Let $\mathcal{M}^c = (W^c, \preceq^c, R_{\BoxS}^c, R_{\pi_F}^c, V^c)$ be the Henkin canonical model of $\LiMSL$ over maximal $k$-consistent theories (Thm. 1.19).
**Conjecture:** There exists a **fully faithful realization functor**:
$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{realize}} \colon \mathcal{M}^c \longrightarrow \mathbf{Sh}(\Ctxadm, \Jsyn)
$$
mapping each prime theory $\Delta \in W^c$ to an admissible structured context $U_\Delta \in \Ctxadm$ such that modal Kripke forcing coincides with internal Kripke–Joyal sheaf forcing:
$$
(\Delta, k) \models \psi \iff U_\Delta \Vdash \psi
$$
establishing that $\LiMSL$ is the complete, internal modal logic of $\Esyn$.
:::

::: {.scholium-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof Reduction Strategy &amp; Horizon Payoff (Conjecture 1):**
* **Step 1:** Construct the syntactic category $\SynCat$ whose objects are deductive theories $(S(x),\Gamma)$ and whose morphisms are provable sequents modulo cut-elimination.
* **Step 2:** Define a canonical Grothendieck coverage $\Jproof$ on $\SynCat$ whose covering sieves correspond to disjunctive proof trees and Fischer–Servi modal confluence paths.
* **Step 3:** Apply **Joyal's Representation Theorem** for Grothendieck toposes to construct the fully faithful embedding $\Phi_{\mathrm{realize}}$.
* **Horizon Payoff:** Unifies Heim's multi-leveled structural logic with Grothendieck Topos Theory, providing a universally sound, machine-checkable foundation for automated theorem provers on context-dependent physics.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Conjecture 2 (§15.4.2): Non-Trivial 12D Metric Null-Space &amp; $R_6$ Condensation**
Let $\operatorname{Met}(R_{12})$ and $\operatorname{Conn}(R_{12})$ be the Fréchet spaces of non-Hermitian metrics and affine connections on $R_{12} = R_4 \times S_2 \times I_6$, and let ${}^4\mathbf{F} \colon \operatorname{Conn}(R_{12}) \times \operatorname{Met}(R_{12}) \to \ell^\infty(\Mtau^{12}, \operatorname{End}(\Lambda^2\mathbb{R}^{12}))$ be the metronized curvature compressor (SM Eq. 100).
**Conjecture:**
1. The solution variety $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{matter}} \coloneqq \{(g,\nabla) \mid {}^4\mathbf{F}(g,\nabla) = \mathbf{0}\}$ is non-empty and decomposes into a discrete family of compact 6D sub-manifolds $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$, forcing **spontaneous geometric compactification** of the informational sub-bundle $I_6$.

::: {.scholium-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof Reduction Strategy &amp; Horizon Payoff (Conjecture 2):**

::: {.thm-box}
**Conjecture 3 (§15.4.3): The Discrete Metronic Mass Gap**
On the discrete metronic spacetime lattice $\Mtau^4 \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ ($\tau > 0$) with difference Laplacian $\Delta_\tau \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^4 \nabla_i^*\nabla_i$ on $\ell^2(\Mtau^4)$ and discrete Yang–Mills Hamiltonian $H_\tau \coloneqq \Delta_\tau + V_{\mathrm{gauge}}$, for any compact non-Abelian gauge group $G$, $\sigma(H_\tau)$ exhibits a strictly positive uniform spectral gap above vacuum $\lambda_0$:
$$
\inf_{\tau > 0} \dist\!\left(\lambda_0(H_\tau),\; \sigma(H_\tau)\setminus\{\lambda_0\}\right) = m_0 c^2 \ge \frac{\hbar c}{\sqrt{\tau}} > 0
$$
* **Reduction Strategy:** Compact Brillouin torus $\mathbb{T}^4 = [-\pi/\tau,\pi/\tau]^4$ gives intrinsic UV cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}}\sim 1/\sqrt{\tau}$; transfer-matrix spectral bounds &amp; discrete Osterwalder–Schrader reflection positivity yield exponential correlation decay $\langle \mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}(0)\mathbf{\Omega}_{\mathrm{int}}(x)\rangle \le C e^{-m_0\|x\|}$.

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Conjecture 4 (§15.4.4): Dynamic Negentropy Flux on $S_2(x_5,x_6)$**
Along any televariant trajectory $\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{tele}}(t)$ satisfying $\dot{V} \le -\gamma V$ (Thm. 6.14), the Lie derivative of Boltzmann entropy $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{therm}}$ along entelechial vector field $X_5 \coloneqq \partial/\partial x_5$ satisfies:

$$
* **Reduction Strategy:** Couple ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$ on $R_4\times S_2$ to stress-energy-entropy $S^\mu = s\cdot u^\mu$; anti-Hermitian connection $\Gamma_{(-)}$ with $[\partial_5,\partial_6]$ acts as an entropy sink pumping negentropy into $R_4$.

## Appendix A (§A.1–A.2): Stratified Syntax & Sequent Calculus of $\LiMSL$ {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">APPENDIX A (§A.1–A.2): CONSTRUCTIVE PROOF THEORY, GRAMMAR (DEF. A.1), RANK METRIC (DEF. A.2) &amp; SEQUENT CALCULUS</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**§A.1 Stratified Grammar of $\WFFiMSL$ (Def. A.1) &amp; Rank Metric (Def. A.2):**
* **Constructive Imperative:** In $\Esyn$, truth is local ($\phi \vee \neg\phi \not\equiv \top$); derivations must trace back to apodictic identifiers $\mathbf{AP}_0 = \{a_0,\dots,a_N\}$ and aspect atoms $\mathbf{AP}_S = \{p_0,p_1,\dots\}$ without circular detours.
* **Generative Term Hierarchy (Def. A.1):**
  $$
  \operatorname{Gen}_0 \coloneqq \mathbf{AP}_0 \sqcup \mathbf{AP}_S, \quad \operatorname{Gen}_{j+1} \coloneqq \big\{\operatorname{Conj}(\phi,\psi),\, \operatorname{Lift}_{\mathrm{syn}}(\phi),\, \operatorname{ParaConj}(\phi) \;\big|\; \phi,\psi\in\operatorname{Gen}_j\big\}
  $$
  $$
  \mathbf{Prop}_k \coloneqq \bigcup_{j=0}^k \operatorname{Gen}_j, \quad \phi,\psi \Coloneqq P \mid \bot \mid \phi\wedge\psi \mid \phi\vee\psi \mid \phi\to\psi \mid \Stable_k(P) \mid \BoxS\phi \mid \DiaS\phi \mid [\pi_F]\phi \mid \langle\pi_F\rangle\phi
  $$
* **Formula Complexity Rank $\rk(\phi)$ &amp; Assertion Level $\lvl(\phi)$ (Def. A.2):**
  $$
  \rk(P) = \rk(\bot) \coloneqq 1, \quad \rk(\phi\circ\psi) \coloneqq \max(\rk(\phi),\rk(\psi))+1
  $$
  $$
  \rk(\BoxS\phi) = \rk(\DiaS\phi) = \rk([\pi_F]\phi) = \rk(\langle\pi_F\rangle\phi) \coloneqq \rk(\phi)+1, \quad \rk(\Stable_k(P)) \coloneqq 2^k + \deg(P) + 2
  $$
  The lexicographic pair $(\lvl(\phi), \rk(\phi)) \in \mathbb{N}_0 \times \mathbb{N}$ forms a strictly well-founded induction metric.
:::

::: {.column width="53%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**§A.2 Single-Succedent Constructive Sequent Calculus ($S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi$):**
Enforces constructive single-succedent discipline across 6 rule strata:

1. **Structural Rules:**
   $\frac{}{S(x);\Gamma,\phi\vdash^k\phi}(\text{Ax})$, $\frac{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi}{S(x);\Gamma,\psi\vdash^k\phi}(\text{W})$, $\frac{S(x);\Gamma,\psi,\psi\vdash^k\phi}{S(x);\Gamma,\psi\vdash^k\phi}(\text{C})$, $\frac{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\psi \quad S(x);\Delta,\psi\vdash^k\phi}{S(x);\Gamma,\Delta\vdash^k\phi}(\text{Cut})$
2. **Intuitionistic Propositional Rules:**
   $(\wedge R), (\wedge L), (\vee R_i), (\vee L), (\bot L), (\to R): \frac{S(x);\Gamma,\phi\vdash^k\psi}{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi\to\psi}, (\to L): \frac{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi \quad S(x);\Delta,\psi\vdash^k\chi}{S(x);\Gamma,\Delta,\phi\to\psi\vdash^k\chi}$
3. **Aspectual Interface with $S_{\mathrm{mod}}(x)$:**
   $\frac{(S_{\mathrm{mod}}(x),k)\models p\;(p\in\mathbf{AP}_S)}{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k p}(\text{Fact-S}_A)$, $\quad\frac{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k(d_r,v_{dr}) \quad S(x);\Delta\vdash^k(f_q,v_{fq})\;[\operatorname{Strength}>\theta_{\mathrm{coord}}]}{S(x);\Gamma,\Delta\vdash^k\operatorname{Coord}((d_r,v_{dr}),(f_q,v_{fq}))}(\chi\text{-I}_S)$
4. **Fischer–Servi Modal Rules:**
   $\frac{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi}{S(x);\BoxS\Gamma\vdash^k\BoxS\phi}(\BoxS K)$, $\frac{S(x);\BoxS\Gamma,\phi\vdash^k\DiaS\psi}{S(x);\BoxS\Gamma,\DiaS\phi\vdash^k\DiaS\psi}(\DiaS K)$, $\frac{S(x);\BoxS\Gamma\vdash^k\phi\to\psi}{S(x);\DiaS\Gamma\vdash^k\DiaS\phi\to\DiaS\psi}(\text{FS-Int})$, $(\BoxS\text{-Ref}), (\DiaS\text{-Ref}), (B_{\Diamond\text{-Adj}})$
5. **Hereditary Stability Rules:**
   $(\operatorname{Stab}_0 R)$, $\frac{P'\in\operatorname{Gen}_{j+1}\;\;S(x);\Gamma\vdash^{j+1}P'\;\;(S(x);\Gamma|_{\le j}\vdash^j\Stable_j(X))_{\operatorname{IGP}}}{S(x);\Gamma\vdash^{j+1}\Stable_{j+1}(P')}(\operatorname{Stab}_{j+1}R)$, $(\operatorname{Stab}L_1)$, $(\operatorname{Stab}L_2)$
6. **Deterministic Dynamic Modality Rules:**
   $(K_{\pi_F}), (\text{MP}_{\pi_F}), (\langle\pi_F\rangle FI), ([\pi_F]\Box_{\mathrm{Syn}}P), ([\pi_F]\leftrightarrow\langle\pi_F\rangle), ([\pi_F]\text{-App}), \frac{S(x);[\pi_F]\Gamma\vdash^k[\pi_F]\theta}{k+1;\Gamma\vdash\theta}([\pi_F]\text{-Step/Unstep})$
:::

:::

Appendix A Sections A.1 and A.2 establish the complete proof-theoretic syntax of L_iMSL, the exponential rank measure rk(Stable_k(P)) = 2^k + deg(P) + 2, and all six families of single-succedent constructive inference rules.

## Appendix A (§A.3): Syntactic Cut Elimination (Gentzen's *Hauptsatz*) {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">APPENDIX A (§A.3): DERIVATION HEIGHT (DEF. A.3), PERMUTATION (LEM. A.4), PRINCIPAL REDUCTION (LEM. A.5) &amp; HAUPTSATZ (THM. A.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Derivation Height $|\mathcal{D}|$ (Def. A.3) &amp; Cut Permutation Lemma (Lem. A.4):**
* **Height $|\mathcal{D}|$:** $0$ on axioms $(\text{Ax}), (\text{Fact-S}_A), (\bot L)$; $|\mathcal{D}_1|+1$ on unary rules; $\max(|\mathcal{D}_1|,|\mathcal{D}_2|)+1$ on binary rules.
* **Lemma A.4 (Cut Permutation):** If cut formula $\psi$ is not principal in the final rule of $\mathcal{D}_1$ or $\mathcal{D}_2$, the Cut permutes upward to sub-derivations with strictly smaller height sum $|\mathcal{D}_1'|+|\mathcal{D}_2'| < |\mathcal{D}_1|+|\mathcal{D}_2|$:
  - *Case 1 (Left rules on $\Delta$):* Permute Cut above $(\wedge L, \vee L, \to L)$ on auxiliary $\chi \in \Delta$; height drops to $|\mathcal{D}_{2a}| = |\mathcal{D}_2|-1$.
  - *Case 2 (Right rules on $\phi$):* Permute Cut across premises $\mathcal{D}_{2a}, \mathcal{D}_{2b}$ of $(\wedge R)$.
  - *Case 3 (Dynamic shift $[\pi_F]\text{-Step}$):* Preserves structure since $\operatorname{Ext}_{[\pi_F]}(\Gamma,\Delta) = \operatorname{Ext}_{[\pi_F]}(\Gamma)\cup\operatorname{Ext}_{[\pi_F]}(\Delta)$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Lemma A.5 (Principal Reduction) &amp; Theorem A.6 (Gentzen's *Hauptsatz*):**
If $\psi$ is principal in both $\mathcal{D}_1$ and $\mathcal{D}_2$, the Cut on $\psi$ reduces to Cuts on strictly lower-rank $\psi'$ ($\rk(\psi') < \rk(\psi)$):
1. **Conjunction ($\psi_1\wedge\psi_2$, Fig. 45):** Replace $(\wedge R)+(\wedge L)$ cut with sequential cuts on $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ plus Contraction $(\text{C})$.
2. **Implication ($\psi_1\to\psi_2$):** Cut $\mathcal{D}_{2a}\vdash\psi_1$ with $\mathcal{D}_{1a}:\Gamma,\psi_1\vdash\psi_2$, then cut $\psi_2$ with $\mathcal{D}_{2b}:\Delta',\psi_2\vdash\phi$.
3. **Disjunction ($\psi_1\vee\psi_2$):** Select matching premise $\mathcal{D}_{2i}:\Delta,\psi_i\vdash^k\phi$ for $(\vee R_i)$ premise $\Gamma\vdash^k\psi_i$.
4. **Modal Necessity ($\BoxS\theta$):** Apply $(\BoxS\text{-Ref})$ iteratively to $\Gamma_0$ in $\mathcal{D}_{1a}:\Gamma_0\vdash^k\theta$ to get $\mathcal{D}_{1a}':\BoxS\Gamma_0\vdash^k\theta$, then cut directly on $\theta$ with $\mathcal{D}_{2a}:\Delta,\theta\vdash^k\phi$ ($\rk(\theta) < \rk(\BoxS\theta)$).
5. **Dynamic ($[\pi_F]\theta$), Stability ($\operatorname{Stable}_{j+1}(P')$) &amp; Possibility ($\Diamond_S\theta$):** Cut at level $k+1$ on $\theta$ via $([\pi_F]\text{-Unstep})$; reduce $\operatorname{Stable}_{j+1}(\operatorname{Lift}_{\BoxS}(P))$ directly to $\operatorname{Stable}_j(P)$; dualize $(\Diamond_S\text{-Ref})$ across $\BoxS\Gamma_0,\theta\vdash^k\Diamond_S\phi$.
* **Theorem A.6 (Cut Elimination):** By double induction on $(\rk(\psi), |\mathcal{D}_1|+|\mathcal{D}_2|) \in \mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}_0$, every derivable sequent $S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi$ has a pure **cut-free derivation** $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{norm}}$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

## Appendix A (§A.4–A.5): Structural Metatheorems & Joyal Representation {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">APPENDIX A (§A.4–A.5): SUBFORMULA (THM. A.7), CONSISTENCY (COR. A.8), DISJUNCTION (THM. A.9) &amp; JOYAL COMPLETENESS (THM. A.12)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**§A.4 Constructive Structural Metatheorems (Thms. A.7–A.9):**
* **Theorem A.7 (Subformula Property):** Every formula $\theta$ occurring in any sequent of a cut-free derivation of $S(x);\Gamma\vdash^k\phi$ is a syntactic subformula of $\Gamma \cup \{\phi\} \cup \mathbf{AP}_0$.
  *Proof:* By inspection of all non-Cut rules in §A.2 and induction on cut-free derivation height $|\mathcal{D}|$. $\blacksquare$
* **Corollary A.8 (Absolute Syntactic Consistency):**
  $$
  S(x);\; \emptyset \nvdash^k \bot
  $$
  *Proof:* Suppose a cut-free derivation $\mathcal{D}$ of $S(x);\emptyset\vdash^k\bot$ exists. $(\text{Ax})$ and left rules require $\Gamma\ne\emptyset$; $(\text{Fact-S}_A)$ derives $p\in\mathbf{AP}_S\ne\bot$; all right rules conclude with compound formulas $\ne\bot$. Contradiction! $\blacksquare$
* **Theorem A.9 (Constructive Disjunction Property):**
  $$
  S(x);\;\emptyset \vdash^k \phi_1 \vee \phi_2 \implies S(x);\;\emptyset \vdash^k \phi_1 \quad\text{or}\quad S(x);\;\emptyset \vdash^k \phi_2
  $$
  *Proof:* With $\Gamma=\emptyset$, the final cut-free inference must be $(\vee R_1)$ or $(\vee R_2)$, whose premise directly proves $\phi_1$ or $\phi_2$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**§A.5 Syntactic Category (Def. A.10) &amp; FS1 Frame Saturation (Lem. A.11):**
* **Def. A.10 ($\SynCat$):** Objects are deductive theories $(S(x),\Gamma)$; morphisms $[\theta]\colon (S(x),\Gamma)\to (S(y),\Delta)$ are cut-free proof equivalence classes deriving $S(y);\Delta\vdash^k\bigwedge\Gamma$ with composition $[\theta_2]\circ[\theta_1] \coloneqq [\operatorname{Cut}(\theta_1,\theta_2)]_{\mathrm{norm}}$.
* **Lemma A.11 (Fischer–Servi FS1 Canonical Frame Saturation):** If $\Delta_1\subseteq\Delta_2$ and $w_1 R^c w_3$, then $\Sigma \coloneqq \Delta_2^{\BoxS}\cup\Delta_3$ is $k$-consistent (by $(\text{FS-Int})$) and extends to prime saturated $w_4=(\Delta_4,k)$ with $w_2 R^c w_4$ and $w_3\preceq^c w_4$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem A.12: Conditional Joyal Representation (Fig. 46)**
Given a site morphism $F \colon (\SynCat, \Jproof) \to (\Ctxadm, \Jsyn)$ preserving covering families and finite limits ($\mathsf{Stratum}=\mathbf{B}, \mathsf{Status}=\mathbf{S_1}, \mathsf{Evid}=\mathbf{E_3}$):
1. **Exactness &amp; Beck–Chevalley:** The representation functor $\Phi_F \colon \SynCat \to \Esyn$ preserves $\Sigma_f \dashv f^* \dashv \Pi_f$, binary products $\Phi_{\mathrm{Joyal}}(\phi\wedge\psi)\cong \Phi_{\mathrm{Joyal}}(\phi)\times_{\mathbf{y}(U)}\Phi_{\mathrm{Joyal}}(\psi)$, equalizers (by subcanonicity of $\Jsyn$), and pullback base-change:
   $$
   \big(g^*\Sigma_f(\llbracket\phi\rrbracket)\big)(X) = \big\{(x_1,x_2)\in V_1\times_U V_2 \;\big|\; x_2\in\llbracket\phi\rrbracket\big\} = \big(\Sigma_{\pi_1}\pi_2^*(\llbracket\phi\rrbracket)\big)(X)
   $$
2. **Bidirectional Completeness (conditional on conservativity of $\Phi_F$):**
   $$
   S(x);\;\Gamma \vdash^k \phi \iff U_{S(x)} \Vdash \left(\bigwedge\Gamma \to \phi\right)
   $$
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Claim Ceiling ($c_{\mathrm{JOYAL}}$) &amp; Appendix A Synthesis (§A.6):**
Topos-theoretic completeness is conditional on the explicitly supplied site morphism $F$ and conservativity theorem:
$$
\mathcal{D} \xrightarrow{\text{Thm. A.6}} \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{norm}} \xrightarrow{\text{Thm. A.7}} \text{Subformula Prop.} \xrightarrow{\text{Cor. A.8 / Thm. A.9}} \nvdash^k\bot \;\wedge\; \text{Disjunction Prop.} \xrightarrow{\text{Thm. A.12}} U_{S(x)}\Vdash(\textstyle\bigwedge\Gamma\to\phi)
$$

**§B.4 Discrete Fine-Structure Constant with Sphere Packing (Thm. B.5):**
On the spatial metronic lattice $\Mtau^3$ with cell area $\tau \approx 1.13115\times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2$, electron reduced Compton wavelength $\lambda_C = \frac{\hbar}{m_e c} \approx 3.86159\times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{m}$, and maximal face-centered cubic (FCC) sphere-packing fraction $f_{\mathrm{pack}} \coloneqq \frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.74048$:
1. **Discrete Geometric Coulomb Rotor Packing Correction ($\gamma_{\text{hex}} = 4/9$, $\alpha_0 = 1/137$):**
   $$
   \eta_{\text{cell}} \coloneqq 1 + \gamma_{\text{hex}}\,f_{\text{pack}}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8\pi}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{8}{\pi}}\,\alpha_0\right)\!\left(1 - \frac{\alpha_0}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right) = 1 + \frac{\sqrt{3/\pi}}{27}\,\alpha_0\!\left(1 - \frac{\alpha_0}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right) \approx 1 + 2.63095\times 10^{-4}
   $$
2. **Exact FCC Metronic Evaluation:**
   $$
   \alpha_{\text{met}}^{-1} \coloneqq 137.000 \cdot \eta_{\text{cell}} \approx \mathbf{137.036044}
   $$
   matching $\alpha_{\text{CODATA}}^{-1} = 137.035999084(21)$ to within $3.3\times 10^{-7}$ relative precision ($\mathsf{Stratum}=\mathbf{C}, \mathsf{Type}=\mathbf{P}, \mathsf{Role}=\text{Bridge}$).

**§B.5 Symplectic Verlet Integrator on $\Mtau^4$ (Def. B.7) &amp; Orbital Precession (Prop. B.8):**
* **Central Verlet Lattice Geodesic Stencil (Def. B.7):** For integer lattice coordinates $n^i(m) \in \mathbb{Z}$ at step $m \in \mathbb{N}_0$:
  $$
  n^i(m+1) = 2n^i(m) - n^i(m-1) - \sum_{k,l=1}^4 \frac{\alpha_k\alpha_l}{\alpha_i}\Big(n^k(m)-n^k(m-1)\Big)\Big(n^l(m)-n^l(m-1)\Big)\Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}(m))

  In the spherically symmetric Schwarzschild–Heim metric $g_{00} = -(1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r})$, $g_{rr} = (1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r})^{-1}$:
